title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and Cervical Cancer: An Exploratory Systematic Review of Heterogeneous Evidence on Epidemiology, Vaccination, Screening, and Molecular Advances.
abstract: This systematic review evaluated evidence on HPV epidemiology, vaccination, screening, and factors associated with cervical cancer and other HPV-related malignancies. Fourteen heterogeneous studies published between 2010 and 2025 were included. HPV16 remained the most frequently reported genotype, while several studies indicated increasing prevalence of other high-risk genotypes, supporting the potential value of the 9-valent HPV vaccine. Population-based evidence demonstrated reduced cervical cancer incidence among women vaccinated before adolescence. Limited studies also investigated HPV persistence, viral load, microbiome alterations, and vaccine awareness. Considering the small number and diversity of studies, findings should be interpreted cautiously and considered exploratory.

title: NF-κB signaling in persistent high-risk cervical HPV infection: Clinical evidence, molecular mechanisms, and translational therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is the essential precursor to cervical carcinogenesis and remains a major global health challenge despite advances in vaccination and screening. While most cervical HPV infections are spontaneously cleared, a subset persists and progresses to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and ultimately invasive cervical cancer. Emerging evidence identifies nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) as a central regulator linking antiviral immunity, chronic inflammation, epithelial survival, and disease progression. In this hybrid review, we systematically synthesize clinical evidence regarding NF-κB activation in persistent cervical high-risk HPV infection and integrate mechanistic insights from molecular studies to develop a translational framework for therapeutic intervention. Current data suggest that HPV oncoproteins E6 and E7 selectively reprogram NF-κB signaling, attenuating antiviral interferon responses while maintaining inflammatory pathways that favor viral persistence and immune dysregulation. A stage-dependent model emerges in which early suppression of antiviral signaling is followed by chronic low-grade NF-κB activation, promoting epithelial survival, microenvironmental remodeling, and progression toward high-grade CIN. We further discuss pathway-specific therapeutic opportunities, including selective NF-κB modulation and integration with therapeutic E6/E7 vaccination. Collectively, NF-κB represents a promising biomarker and therapeutic target for host-directed strategies aimed at viral clearance and prevention of cervical cancer progression.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of NF-κB signaling in persistent high-risk HPV infection, focusing on its implications in cervical carcinogenesis. The study highlights how HPV oncoproteins E6 and E7 reprogram NF-κB to suppress antiviral responses while sustaining inflammation, which supports viral persistence and immune dysregulation. A stage-dependent model is proposed, where early antiviral suppression transitions to chronic low-grade NF-κB activation, facilitating epithelial survival and progression to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). The review emphasizes the potential of targeting NF-κB pathways for therapeutic interventions, including selective modulation and E6/E7 vaccination strategies. Despite the insights, the evidence remains limited, and further research is needed to validate these approaches and address gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms of NF-κB's role in HPV-associated diseases.

title: Trends in sociodemographic factors associated with human papillomavirus vaccine hesitancy in the United States: 2010-2022.
abstract: Abstract Background Previous studies suggest that rates of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine hesitancy vary by adolescent and parent sociodemographic characteristics. This study assessed trends in the characteristics of parents who did not intend to have their child vaccinated for HPV in the United States. Methods The authors used data from the 2010–2022 National Immunization Survey–Teen among adolescents who had received zero doses of the HPV vaccine. Vaccine hesitancy was assessed with the question “How likely is it that your teen will receive HPV shots in the next 12 months?” Parents who responded with “not too likely, “not likely at all,” or “not sure/don't know” were deemed vaccine hesitant. Joinpoint regression estimated yearly increases and/or decreases in vaccine hesitancy by adolescent and mother characteristics through annual percent changes. Results A total of 204,196 unvaccinated adolescents were included in the study, 66.0% had parents who were classified as HPV vaccine hesitant. Overall, the proportion of adolescents with mothers who were HPV vaccine hesitant declined from 72% in 2010 to 61% in 2022. Among parents with female children, HPV vaccine hesitancy decreased significantly from 2010 to 2012, increased significantly from 2012 to 2018 followed by a significant decrease from 2018 to 2022. Among parents with male children, HPV vaccine hesitancy decreased significantly from 2010 to 2012 and remained stable from 2012 to 2022. Parents with children of all racial and ethnic groups experienced significant decreases in HPV vaccine hesitancy from 2010 to 2012 and then remained stable from 2012 to 2022. Conclusions This study emphasizes the need to dispel misconceptions and create awareness about HPV vaccine across all strata of the society.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 以往研究表明,与青少年及家长社会人口学特征相关的人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗犹豫率存在差异。本研究评估了美国未计划为其子女接种HPV疫苗的家长特征的变化趋势。方法 研究者使用了2010–2022年国家青少年免疫接种调查(National Immunization Survey–Teen)的数据,调查对象为未接种过HPV 疫苗的青少年。通过问题“您的青少年在未来12个月内接种HPV疫苗的可能性有多大?”来评估疫苗犹豫情况。回答为“不太可能”、“完全不可能”或“不确定/不知道”的家长被归类为疫苗犹豫。使用Joinpoint回归分析,通过年度百分比变化估计每年疫苗犹豫率的变化趋势。结果 本研究共纳入204,196名未接种疫苗的青少年,其中66.0%的家长被归类为HPV 疫苗犹豫。总体而言,母亲被归类为HPV 疫苗犹豫的青少年比例从2010年的72%下降到2022年的61%。对于有女孩子的家长,HPV 疫苗犹豫率在2010年至2012年间显著下降,随后在2012年至2018年间显著上升,再从2018年至2022年间显著下降。对于有男孩子的家长,HPV 疫苗犹豫率在2010年至2012年间显著下降,并在2012年至2022年间保持稳定。所有种族和民族背景的家长在2010年至2012年间都经历了HPV 疫苗犹豫率的显著下降,之后在2012年至2022年间保持稳定。结论 本研究强调需要消除关于HPV 疫苗的误解,并在社会各阶层中提高对其的认识。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 提供的证据未报告与HPV 疫苗犹豫相关的具体争议或证据缺口。本研究提供了趋势信息,但未涉及矛盾发现或未解决的机制。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本研究强调需要消除关于HPV 疫苗的误解,并在社会各阶层中提高对其的认识。

title: Knowledge and attitudes of medical students about human papillomavirus (HPV) and HPV vaccine: A cross-sectional survey in Inner Mongolia, China.
abstract: China approved human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines for women and men in 2016 and 2025 respectively. We aimed to online survey the knowledge of HPV and HPV vaccines, as well as the vaccine uptake, among medical college students in Inner Mongolia, during April 1-21, 2026. Of 5,846 eligible students, 660 (11.3%) participated in the survey. Fourteen respondents were excluded because of their incomplete questionnaires. Of 646 respondents aged 20.5 (±1.5) years with 65.5% (423) females, 93.6% and 87.6% were aware of HPV and HPV vaccines respectively. However, only 74.8% of them knew HPV as the main cause of cervical cancer and 73.5% knew the preventive effect of HPV vaccines against cervical cancer. Fewer respondents knew the association of HPV with other cancers. The males had less knowledge than females. Only 115 (27.2%) females had received HPV vaccination, and none of the males did due to transient availability of the vaccine for males. Family income, paternal education, and HPV vaccine knowledge were the main factors associated with the vaccination. The vaccination barriers included vaccine cost, perceived lack of necessity, doubts about effectiveness, concerns about adverse events, and unawareness of where to get vaccinated. Among the unvaccinated respondents, 61.4% (137/223) of the males and 86.4% (266/308) of the females intended to get vaccinated. The survey revealed gaps in HPV and HPV vaccine knowledge, as well as low vaccination coverage among medical students. The results indicate that enhancing education about HPV and HPV vaccines appears valuable for increasing HPV vaccine uptake.

title: Oncogenic role of human papillomavirus in oral and oropharyngeal cancers: Molecular insights and clinical implications for dental practice.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) has emerged as a distinct and rising subset of head and neck malignancy, yet awareness among dental care practitioners remains limited. The authors synthesized the molecular biology of HPV-driven oral and oropharyngeal carcinogenesis, the diagnostic frameworks, and the evidence base for an expanded dental care practitioner role in detection, counseling, and prevention. TYPES OF STUDIES REVIEWED: A structured literature search of PubMed-indexed English-language articles through March 2026 was conducted using search terms including HPV, oropharyngeal cancer, oral squamous cell carcinoma, p16 immunohistochemistry, HPV vaccination, and dental practice. Original research, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, and population-level surveillance data were selected, with an emphasis on studies reporting clinical, diagnostic, or prevention outcomes applicable to dental settings. The authors did not include single case reports or small case series, and they excluded conference abstracts, editorials, and articles not available in the English language. RESULTS: HPV type 16 drives from 70% through 90% of HPV-positive OPSCCs through E6-mediated p53 degradation and E7-mediated retinoblastoma protein inactivation. HPV-positive OPSCC carries a better prognosis than HPV-negative disease but lacks a clinically identifiable premalignant phase and typically manifests at an advanced locoregional stage. P16 immunohistochemistry has reduced specificity in the oral cavity and tobacco-predominant populations. Prophylactic HPV vaccination had an 88% reduction in vaccine-type oral HPV prevalence among vaccinated young adults. CONCLUSIONS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Dental care practitioners can contribute meaningfully to earlier detection through systematic clinical examination, cervical lymph node palpation, timely specialist referral, patient counseling on HPV transmission, and vaccination advocacy.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 通过2026年3月的PubMed索引英文文章进行结构化文献检索,重点关注在牙科环境中具有临床、诊断或预防结果的研究。

CONCLUSIONS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Dental care practitioners can contribute meaningfully to earlier detection through systematic clinical examination, cervical lymph node palpation, timely specialist referral, patient counseling on HPV transmission, and vaccination advocacy.
abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)阳性口咽部鳞状细胞癌(OPSCC)已成为头颈恶性肿瘤中一个独特且日益增多的亚型,但牙科护理人员对此的认知仍较为有限。作者综合了HPV驱动的口腔及口咽部癌变的分子生物学机制、诊断框架以及支持扩大牙科护理人员在检测、咨询和预防方面作用的证据基础。回顾的研究类型:通过结构化的文献检索,使用包括HPV、口咽癌、口腔鳞状细胞癌、p16免疫组化、HPV 疫苗接种、以及牙科实践等关键词,在PubMed索引的英文文章中进行了至2026年3月的搜索。选取了原始研究、系统综述、临床指南和人群层面的监测数据,特别关注在牙科环境中具有临床、诊断或预防结果的研究。作者未纳入单个病例报告或小病例系列,并排除了会议摘要、社论以及非英文文章。结果:HPV 16型通过E6介导的p53降解和E7介导的视网膜母细胞瘤蛋白失活,驱动了70%至90%的HPV阳性OPSCC。HPV阳性OPSCC的预后优于HPV阴性疾病,但缺乏可临床识别的癌前阶段,通常表现为局部晚期病变。p16免疫组化在口腔和以烟草为主的群体中特异性较低。预防性HPV 疫苗接种在接种疫苗的年轻成人中,将疫苗型口腔HPV 患病率减少了88%。结论与实际意义:牙科护理人员可以通过系统的临床检查、颈部淋巴结触诊、及时转诊专科医生、对HPV 传播进行患者咨询以及推动疫苗接种的倡导,有意义地促进早期检测。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决牙科从业人员对HPV阳性口咽鳞状细胞癌的认知不足问题,该疾病是头颈恶性肿瘤中一个独特且日益增多的亚型。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 通过2026年3月的PubMed索引英文文章进行结构化文献检索,重点关注在牙科环境中具有临床、诊断或预防结果的研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者回顾了原始研究、系统综述、临床指南和人口水平的监测数据,排除了单个病例报告、小病例系列和非英文文章。
analysis_zh.main_results: HPV 16型通过E6介导的p53降解和E7介导的视网膜母细胞瘤蛋白失活,导致约70%至90%的HPV阳性口咽癌(OPSCC)。HPV阳性OPSCC的预后优于HPV阴性疾病,但缺乏可临床识别的癌前阶段,通常表现为局部晚期病变。P16免疫组化在口腔和烟草主导人群中特异性降低。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为HPV16是HPV阳性OPSCC的主要驱动因素,并指出牙科从业人员可以通过系统的临床检查、颈部淋巴结触诊、及时转诊专科医生、对HPV 传播进行患者咨询以及推动疫苗接种,有意义地促进早期检测。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 牙科从业人员可以在HPV阳性OPSCC的检测、咨询和预防中发挥重要作用,而HPV阳性OPSCC的预后优于HPV阴性疾病。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究的局限性包括排除了单个病例报告和小病例系列,以及依赖英文文章。由于采用了结构化文献检索并纳入了多种类型的研究,证据强度中等。

title: Mutations in High-Risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Genotypes: Implications for Genetic Variability and Its Relationship with Cervical Cancer
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) remains the principal etiological agent of cervical cancer, accounting for more than 95% of cases worldwide. Although the carcinogenic role of high-risk genotypes such as HPV-16 and HPV-18 has been extensively established, growing evidence suggests that genetic variability within individual genotypes may contribute to differences in viral persistence, oncogenic potential, immune evasion, and clinical outcomes. This scoping review aimed to synthesize current evidence regarding intratype mutations, viral lineages, and sublineages of high-risk HPV genotypes and to examine their implications for cervical carcinogenesis, vaccine effectiveness, and molecular diagnosis. A literature search was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR framework using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and supplementary searches and citation tracking. Fifty-four studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. The available evidence suggests considerable genomic heterogeneity among high-risk HPV genotypes, although the strength of the reported associations varies substantially across studies. Several observational studies have suggested that non-European HPV-16 lineages, particularly lineage D sublineages, may be associated with an increased risk of cervical cancer. Mutations affecting the E6, E7, and long control region (LCR) have been reported to be associated with altered viral transcriptional activity, persistence, and oncogenic potential. Genetic variability may influence molecular diagnostic performance and potentially affect vaccine-induced immune responses. However, most reported associations are supported by a limited number of observational studies and should therefore be interpreted with caution. Overall, the available evidence supports the integration of genomic surveillance into HPV prevention and control strategies while highlighting the need for additional high-quality studies to clarify the clinical significance of HPV intratype genomic diversity.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review explores the role of intratype mutations, viral lineages, and sublineages in high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their implications for cervical carcinogenesis, vaccine effectiveness, and molecular diagnosis. The review synthesizes evidence from 54 studies, emphasizing the genomic heterogeneity of high-risk HPV genotypes, particularly HPV-16 and HPV-18. While mutations in E6, E7, and the long control region (LCR) are associated with altered viral activity and oncogenic potential, the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. The review underscores the need for further high-quality research to better understand the clinical significance of these genetic variations and to integrate genomic surveillance into HPV prevention and control strategies.

This scoping review aimed to synthesize current evidence regarding intratype mutations, viral lineages, and sublineages of high-risk HPV genotypes and to examine their implications for cervical carcinogenesis, vaccine effectiveness, and molecular diagnosis. A literature search was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR framework using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and supplementary searches and citation tracking. Fifty-four studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. The available evidence suggests considerable genomic heterogeneity among high-risk HPV genotypes, although the strength of the reported associations varies substantially across studies. Several observational studies have suggested that non-European HPV-16 lineages, particularly lineage D sublineages, may be associated with an increased risk of cervical cancer. Mutations affecting the E6, E7, and long control region (LCR) have been reported to be associated with altered viral transcriptional activity, persistence, and oncogenic potential. Genetic variability may influence molecular diagnostic performance and potentially affect vaccine-induced immune responses. However, most reported associations are supported by a limited number of observational studies and should therefore be interpreted with caution. Overall, the available evidence supports the integration of genomic surveillance into HPV prevention and control strategies while highlighting the need for additional high-quality studies to clarify the clinical significance of HPV intratype genomic diversity.
abstract_zh: 高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)仍是宫颈癌的主要病因,占全球病例的95%以上。尽管高危型基因型如HPV-16和HPV-18的致癌作用已被广泛证实,但越来越多的证据表明,个体基因型内的遗传变异可能影响病毒持续感染、致癌潜力、免疫逃逸和临床结局。本综述旨在综合当前关于高危型HPV内部突变、病毒谱系及其亚谱系的证据,并探讨其对宫颈癌发生、抗病毒药物疗效和分子诊断的影响。文献检索遵循PRISMA-ScR框架,使用PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science以及补充检索和引文追踪。共有54项研究符合纳入标准,并被纳入定性综合分析。现有证据表明,高危型HPV存在显著的基因组异质性,但不同研究中报告的关联强度差异较大。一些观察性研究提示,非欧洲HPV-16谱系,特别是D谱系亚谱系,可能与宫颈癌风险增加相关。影响E6、E7和长控制区(LCR)的遗传变异已被报道与病毒转录活性、持续感染和致癌潜力的变化相关。遗传变异可能影响分子诊断的性能,并可能影响抗病毒药物诱导的治疗效果。然而,大多数报告的关联仅基于有限数量的观察性研究,因此应谨慎解释。总体而言,现有证据支持将抗病毒药物纳入HPV预防和控制策略,同时强调需要更多高质量研究以阐明HPV内部基因组多样性的临床意义。

title: Triptolide as a Chemosensitizer in Human Papillomavirus Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Through TP53.
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the seventh most common cancer globally and has demonstrated an etiological shift over recent decades. Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a key risk factor for HNSCC, and its incidence has been rising since 1980. HPV-associated HNSCC display a unique tumorigenesis process and respond differently to traditional HNSCC treatment. Triptolide, a natural derivative, has shown promise as a chemosensitizer against HPV-positive HNSCC. The aim of this study was to investigate activity of triptolide in HNSCC in addition to in silico analysis of triptolide gene targets. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Effects of triptolide on proliferation of HPV-positive and HPV-negative HNSCC cells were evaluated using an MTT assay in vitro. Effects of triptolide on TP53 promoter activity and phosphorylation of TP53 protein were measured by reporter gene assay and western blot respectively. Next, enrichment of triptolide gene targets was evaluated through cBioPortal and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) with a subsequent STRING analysis. RESULTS: Triptolide acts as a chemosensitizer in combination with low-dose cisplatin. This effect is most pronounced in HPV-positive cells. HPV-positive cells also show increased TP53 promoter activity and TP53 protein phosphorylation. STRING analysis shows involvement of JAK-STAT signaling, interleukin-23 signaling, and apoptosis pathways in HPV-positive samples. In HPV-negative samples, enriched triptolide targets are implicated in RUNX3 regulation of CDKN1A transcription and interleukin-4, interleukin-13, and interleukin-17 signaling. CONCLUSION: Triptolide acts as an in vitro chemosensitizer in HPV-positive HNSCC, likely through reactivation of wild-type TP53 and restoration of apoptotic control. Inflammatory cytokine signaling blockade may provide an additional mechanism contributing to this chemosensitizing effect.

abstract_zh: 背景/目的:头颈鳞状细胞癌(HNSCC)是全球第七常见的癌症,近年来其病因学发生了显著变化。人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒)感染是HNSCC的关键风险因素,其发病率自1980年以来持续上升。与HPV相关的HNSCC表现出独特的肿瘤发生过程,并对传统的HNSCC 治疗治疗反应不同。三尖杉酯碱作为一种天然衍生物,已被证明在HPV阳性HNSCC中具有作为化学增敏剂的潜力。本研究旨在通过体外实验评估三尖杉酯碱在HNSCC中的活性,并结合三尖杉酯碱基因靶点的计算机模拟分析。材料与方法:通过体外MTT实验评估三尖杉酯碱对HPV阳性及HPV阴性HNSCC细胞增殖的影响。通过报告基因实验和Western blot分别检测三尖杉酯碱对TP53启动子活性及TP53蛋白磷酸化的影响。随后,通过cBioPortal和癌症基因组图谱(TCGA)评估三尖杉酯碱基因靶点的富集情况,并进行STRING分析。结果:三尖杉酯碱在与低剂量顺铂联合使用时表现出化学增敏作用,这种作用在HPV阳性细胞中最为显著。HPV阳性细胞还显示出TP53启动子活性增加和TP53蛋白磷酸化增强。STRING分析显示,在HPV阳性样本中,JAK-STAT信号通路、白细胞介素-23信号通路和凋亡通路参与其中。在HPV阴性样本中,三尖杉酯碱靶点的富集与RUNX3调控CDKN1A转录以及白细胞介素-4、白细胞介素-13和白细胞介素-17信号通路相关。结论:三尖杉酯碱在HPV阳性HNSCC中表现出体外化学增敏作用,可能通过重新激活野生型TP53并恢复凋亡控制实现。炎症细胞因子信号通路的阻断可能为这种化学增敏作用提供了额外的机制。科学与公共卫生意义:研究结果表明,三尖杉酯碱可能是一种有前景的化学增敏剂,用于HPV阳性HNSCC的治疗,通过重新激活TP53并恢复凋亡通路,可能改善治疗治疗效果。这可能为未来针对HPV相关癌症的靶向治疗研究提供信息。局限性与证据强度:本研究仅限于体外分析,未包括临床试验或长期结果。由于基于实验室实验和计算分析,而没有直接的临床验证,证据强度中等。

title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination and the Impact of Vaccine Implementation in Kenya: Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary etiological agent of cervical cancer, a disease that remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women in Kenya despite the availability of highly effective prophylactic vaccines. This review examines the current evidence on HPV virology, vaccine immunology, global vaccine effectiveness, and the implementation of HPV vaccination in Kenya following its introduction into the national immunization program in 2019. It also evaluates progress in vaccine delivery, coverage trends, and the adoption of the single-dose vaccination schedule, while highlighting persistent challenges including vaccine hesitancy, inequitable access, health system constraints, and socioeconomic barriers. Available evidence indicates that HPV vaccination has strengthened cervical cancer prevention efforts and has the potential to substantially reduce the future burden of HPV-related disease. However, vaccine coverage remains below the World Health Organization target for cervical cancer elimination, limiting the full public health impact of the program. Key research priorities include evaluating long-term vaccine effectiveness, monitoring HPV genotype dynamics, assessing vaccine performance among people living with HIV, and strengthening the integration of HPV vaccination with cervical cancer screening programs. Achieving equitable vaccine access, enhancing surveillance systems, improving community engagement, and ensuring sustainable financing will be essential to maximizing the benefits of HPV vaccination and accelerating progress toward the elimination of cervical cancer in Kenya.

abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是宫颈癌的主要病因,尽管已有高度有效的预防性疫苗,该疾病仍然是肯尼亚女性癌症相关发病率和死亡率的主要原因。本综述探讨了当前关于HPV病毒学、疫苗免疫学、全球疫苗有效性以及自2019年人乳头瘤病毒疫苗纳入国家免疫计划以来在肯尼亚实施情况的证据。同时,评估了疫苗接种进展、覆盖率趋势以及单剂量疫苗接种方案的采用情况,同时突出了持续存在的挑战,包括疫苗接种犹豫、不平等的获取机会、卫生系统限制以及社会经济障碍。现有证据表明,人乳头瘤病毒疫苗已加强宫颈癌预防工作,并有潜力显著降低未来与HPV相关的疾病负担。然而,疫苗接种覆盖率仍低于世界卫生组织消除宫颈癌的目标,限制了该计划的全部公共卫生影响。关键的研究优先事项包括评估长期疫苗有效性、监测HPV基因型动态、评估HIV感染者中疫苗的表现,以及加强人乳头瘤病毒疫苗与宫颈癌筛查计划的整合。实现公平的疫苗获取、增强卫生系统、提高社区参与度以及确保可持续的资金支持对于最大化人乳头瘤病毒疫苗的效益并加速肯尼亚消除宫颈癌的进程至关重要。

title: HPV16 Genomic Status Stratifies Risk of Disease Recurrence in Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Abstract Purpose: A subset of patients with human papillomavirus (HPV)–positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) develops disease recurrence despite generally favorable outcomes. Reliable biomarkers for risk stratification remain lacking. We investigated whether comprehensive viral genomic profiling refines prognostic classification. Experimental Design: Tumor samples from 100 patients with p16-positive and HPV DNA–positive OPSCC enrolled in 2 independent cohorts were analyzed using targeted viral capture sequencing. Viral genotype, sublineage, single-nucleotide variation, virus–host integration sites, viral structural variants (SV), clonality, and viral copy number were characterized. Associations with cumulative incidence of progression, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival were assessed at 60 months. Results: HPV16 was detected in 94 tumors, 83 of which belonged to the HPV16_A1 sublineage. Within this sublineage, 20 tumors harbored strictly episomal viral genomes, whereas 63 exhibited integration and/or viral SV. No progression events occurred in the strictly episomal HPV16_A1 subgroup, whereas 12 occurred among HPV16_A1 tumors with an integration and/or SV. At 60 months, no progression events were observed in strictly episomal HPV16_A1 tumors compared with a 23.1% cumulative incidence of progression in HPV16_A1 tumors with an integration and/or SV. Previously reported high-risk single-nucleotide variants and a novel upstream regulatory region variant were associated with worse PFS. Integration sites were enriched in open chromatin and promoter regions and clustered within viral E2 and E4 genes. Conclusions: Within HPV16_A1 tumors, viral genomic architecture defines clinically distinct subgroups. Strictly episomal (wild-type) genomes identify a low-risk population, whereas integration and SV characterize higher-risk disease.

title_zh: HPV16基因组状态可区分口咽鳞状细胞癌疾病复发风险
source_body_en: Abstract Purpose: A subset of patients with human papillomavirus (HPV)–positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) develops disease recurrence despite generally favorable outcomes. Reliable biomarkers for risk stratification remain lacking. We investigated whether comprehensive viral genomic profiling refines prognostic classification. Experimental Design: Tumor samples from 100 patients with p16-positive and HPV DNA–positive OPSCC enrolled in 2 independent cohorts were analyzed using targeted viral capture sequencing. Viral genotype, sublineage, single-nucleotide variation, virus–host integration sites, viral structural variants (SV), clonality, and viral copy number were characterized. Associations with cumulative incidence of progression, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival were assessed at 60 months. Results: HPV16 was detected in 94 tumors, 83 of which belonged to the HPV16_A1 sublineage. Within this sublineage, 20 tumors harbored strictly episomal viral genomes, whereas 63 exhibited integration and/or viral SV. No progression events occurred in the strictly episomal HPV16_A1 subgroup, whereas 12 occurred among HPV16_A1 tumors with an integration and/or SV. At 60 months, no progression events were observed in strictly episomal HPV16_A1 tumors compared with a 23.1% cumulative incidence of progression in HPV16_A1 tumors with an integration and/or SV. Previously reported high-risk single-nucleotide variants and a novel upstream regulatory region variant were associated with worse PFS. Integration sites were enriched in open chromatin and promoter regions and clustered within viral E2 and E4 genes. Conclusions: Within HPV16_A1 tumors, viral genomic architecture defines clinically distinct subgroups. Strictly episomal (wild-type) genomes identify a low-risk population, whereas integration and SV characterize higher-risk disease.

title: Fluorescence biosensing for simultaneous detection of HPV16 and HPV18.
abstract: Cervical, most anal, and most oropharyngeal cancers are caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), with HPV16 and HPV18 accounting for the majority of cases, necessitating simultaneous detection of multiple HPV types for identifying HPV infection, risk stratification, and screening for HPV-associated disease. Entropy-driven catalytic strand displacement reactions are DNA self-assembly amplification methods that do not require enzymes for signal amplification. Furthermore, their driving forces originate within the system, endowing them with high specificity, which provides a crucial advantage for simultaneous detection of several targets. Therefore, an analytical method was developed to amplify fluorescence signals via dual-toehold-mediated strand displacement, enabling simultaneous detection of HPV18 and HPV16. For both targets, the established method shows excellent linearity of the regression curve in the concentration range from 0.05 to 5 nM. The detection limits for HPV18 and HPV16 were 0.020 and 0.033 nM, respectively, which are highly favorable even for the detection of only a single HPV type. These results show that the developed enzyme-free assay has high sensitivity and specificity, making it a promising technique for rapid and cost-effective HPV16 and HPV18 screening.

The findings suggest potential applications in improving early detection and risk assessment for HPV-associated cancers, particularly cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. The study does not report limitations, but the high sensitivity and specificity observed support its scientific and public health significance.

abstract_zh: 宫颈癌、大多数肛门癌以及大多数口咽癌是由人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)引起的,其中HPV16和HPV18占大多数病例,因此需要同时检测多种HPV类型以识别HPV感染、进行风险分层和筛查HPV相关疾病。熵驱动的催化链置换反应是基于DNA自组装的信号放大方法,无需酶参与。此外,其驱动力源自系统内部,赋予其高特异性,这对于同时检测多个目标具有关键优势。因此,开发了一种分析方法,通过双脚手架介导的链置换反应放大荧光信号,从而实现对HPV18和HPV16的同时检测。对于这两种目标,该方法在浓度范围0.05至5 nM内表现出良好的回归曲线线性。HPV18和HPV16的检测限分别为0.020和0.033 nM,即使仅用于检测单一HPV类型,这些数值也极具优势。这些结果表明,所开发的无酶检测方法具有高灵敏度和特异性,使其成为快速且经济有效的HPV16和HPV18筛查的有前景技术。

title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adolescent and parent perspectives on human papillomavirus vaccination through the School Immunisation Program in Queensland, Australia: a qualitative study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples experience a greater burden of cervical cancer than other Australians. Vaccination can prevent diseases caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), but uptake remains inequitable. We aimed to understand barriers and enablers influencing the participation of Queensland Aboriginalmed and Torres Strait Islander adolescents in the school-based HPV vaccination program. METHODS: Using an Indigenist research approach and guided by a socio-ecological model for health promotion, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander voices were centred in this project. In 2020-2021 we conducted Yarns (a culturally appropriate qualitative method) with 65 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adolescents and 20 parents from 10 diverse Queensland schools. Yarns addressed understandings of HPV and HPV vaccination, information and resources, vaccine consent, experience of vaccination, and suggestions for improvement. Thematic analysis using a codebook approach was conducted. RESULTS: The first major theme related to factors leading up to the vaccination clinic. Despite varying levels of knowledge and understanding of HPV and HPV vaccination, most adolescents and parents supported the idea of vaccinations to prevent diseases and benefit their health. Adolescents and parents reported difficulties completing and returning the consent form and wanted more accessible information and improved communication about the vaccine, delivered in culturally appropriate ways. The second major theme related to factors on the day of the vaccination clinic. Adolescents reported a need for privacy during vaccination, ways to manage heightened emotions triggered by the vaccination clinic, and the presence of trusted support people. Findings were contextualised within the COVID-19 pandemic and vaccination rollout, with the pandemic causing disruptions to the school program and the HPV vaccine perceived as more trustworthy than the then-new COVID-19 vaccines. CONCLUSIONS: We provide several recommendations to support Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adolescents to be vaccinated against HPV, such as flexible consent processes with assistance from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander support staff; availability of culturally safe educational materials for adolescents, parents and school staff; the presence of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander support staff at clinics, and adherence to optimal clinic set up and scheduling to improve adolescents' experience of vaccination. These recommendations can guide programmatic changes and interventions to increase HPV vaccination rates among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adolescents, thereby advancing equity in cervical cancer outcomes.

title: Human Papillomavirus Condylomas of Extragenital Site in Immunocompetent Man, New York, USA, 2025.
abstract: Human papillomavirus types 6 and 11 are associated with mucosal condylomata acuminata, with rare reports of extragenital manifestations. We report a case of condyloma localized to the neck of an immunocompetent heterosexual man, without concurrent anogenital lesions. Our findings challenge theories of the site-specific tropism of these human papillomavirus types.

title: Disbiosis cervicovaginal asociada a infección y persistencia del Virus del Papiloma Humano en mujeres revisión paraguas, 2019-2025 Cervicovaginal dysbiosis associated with Human Papillomavirus infection and persistence in women: an umbrella review, 2019–2025
abstract: Cervicovaginal dysbiosis has been proposed as a modifiable biological cofactor that may alter the mucosal barrier and inflammatory microenvironment, whereas persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is necessary, but not sufficient, for cervical carcinogenesis. This umbrella review aimed to synthesize and critically appraise evidence from systematic reviews on the relationship between the cervicovaginal microbiota, HPV infection and persistence, and progression to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer. An umbrella review of systematic reviews with or without meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane, LILACS, and Epistemonikos were searched through November 3, 2025, for publications in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. Two reviewers independently performed study selection and methodological appraisal using AMSTAR 2; findings were synthesized narratively and thematically. Eight systematic reviews were included. Bacterial vaginosis, loss of Lactobacillus dominance, and profiles not dominated by L. crispatus, particularly CST IV and communities dominated by L. iners, were associated with a higher likelihood of HPV infection, viral persistence, and high-grade cervical lesions. crispatus-dominated profiles were associated with lower risk. Methodological confidence in the included reviews was predominantly low to moderate, with substantial heterogeneity in populations, definitions of dysbiosis, and microbiological methods. Overall, the evidence supports cervicovaginal dysbiosis as a cofactor associated with the course of HPV infection, but does not establish causality. These findings support the need for longitudinal studies and clinical trials evaluating microbiome-related biomarkers and targeted interventions before their incorporation into clinical, risk-stratified screening, or public health strategies in practice.

analysis.summary_en: This umbrella review synthesizes evidence on the relationship between cervicovaginal dysbiosis, HPV infection, and persistence, and their progression to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer. Methodological confidence in the included systematic reviews was low to moderate, with significant heterogeneity in populations, definitions, and microbiological methods. The findings suggest the need for further research and clinical trials to evaluate microbiome-related biomarkers and interventions for their potential use in risk-stratified screening and public health strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 宫颈阴道菌群失调已被提出为一种可改变的生物学共因子,可能改变黏膜屏障和炎症微环境,而持续的人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染是宫颈癌发生所必需的,但并非充分条件。

title_zh: 与人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染及持续存在相关的宫颈阴道菌群失调:伞状综述,2019–2025
source_body_en: Cervicovaginal dysbiosis has been proposed as a modifiable biological cofactor that may alter the mucosal barrier and inflammatory microenvironment, whereas persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is necessary, but not sufficient, for cervical carcinogenesis. This umbrella review aimed to synthesize and critically appraise evidence from systematic reviews on the relationship between the cervicovaginal microbiota, HPV infection and persistence, and progression to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer. An umbrella review of systematic reviews with or without meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane, LILACS, and Epistemonikos were searched through November 3, 2025, for publications in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. Two reviewers independently performed study selection and methodological appraisal using AMSTAR 2; findings were synthesized narratively and thematically. Eight systematic reviews were included. Bacterial vaginosis, loss of Lactobacillus dominance, and profiles not dominated by L. crispatus, particularly CST IV and communities dominated by L. iners, were associated with a higher likelihood of HPV infection, viral persistence, and high-grade cervical lesions. crispatus-dominated profiles were associated with lower risk. Methodological confidence in the included reviews was predominantly low to moderate, with substantial heterogeneity in populations, definitions of dysbiosis, and microbiological methods. Overall, the evidence supports cervicovaginal dysbiosis as a cofactor associated with the course of HPV infection, but does not establish causality. These findings support the need for longitudinal studies and clinical trials evaluating microbiome-related biomarkers and targeted interventions before their incorporation into clinical, risk-stratified screening, or public health strategies in practice.
abstract_zh: 宫颈阴道菌群失调已被提出为一种可改变的生物学共因子,可能改变黏膜屏障和炎症微环境,而持续的人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染是宫颈癌发生所必需的,但并非充分条件。本伞状综述旨在综合并批判性评估系统综述中关于宫颈阴道菌群、HPV感染及持续存在与进展至宫颈上皮内瘤变和人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)之间的关系的证据。根据PRISMA 2020和PRISMA-S指南,进行了包含系统综述(无论是否包含荟萃分析)的伞状综述。通过2025年11月3日,检索了MEDLINE/PubMed、Embase、Scopus、Web of Science、Cochrane、LILACS和Epistemonikos数据库,以获取英文、西班牙文和葡萄牙文的文献。两名评审员独立进行研究选择和方法学评估,使用AMSTAR 2工具;结果通过叙述性及主题性方式进行综合。共纳入8项系统综述。细菌性阴道病、乳酸杆菌优势丧失以及非L. crispatus主导的菌群特征,特别是CST IV型和由L. iners主导的菌群,与更高的HPV感染、病毒持续存在和高级别宫颈病变风险相关。而由L. crispatus主导的菌群特征则与较低风险相关。纳入的综述方法学信心总体较低至中等,且在人群、菌群失调的定义以及微生物学方法方面存在显著异质性。总体而言,现有证据支持宫颈阴道菌群失调作为与HPV感染过程相关的共因子,但并未确立因果关系。这些发现支持在将其纳入临床、风险分层筛查或公共卫生策略之前,开展纵向研究和临床试验,以评估与菌群相关的生物标志物和针对性干预措施的必要性。

title: Human papillomavirus vaccination readiness, uptake, and perceived barriers among university students in the Pearl River Delta Region: A cross-sectional study
abstract: Introduction: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents cervical cancer and other HPV-related diseases, yet uptake among Chinese university students is uneven. Objective: We examined HPV vaccination readiness, uptake, and perceived barriers among university students in the Pearl River Delta. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional survey in May–June 2026. Outcomes were classified as no definite short-term intention, intention to vaccinate within six months, or vaccinated. We used multinomial and binary logistic regression, a 13-item knowledge score, and an 8-item barrier index. Results: Of 429 students, 175 (40.8%) lacked definite short-term intention, 89 (20.7%) intended to vaccinate within six months, and 165 (38.5%) were vaccinated. Short-term intention was associated with sexual activity with (adjusted OR [aOR] = 4.14, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.20–7.79) or without (aOR = 3.06, 95% CI: 1.12–8.35) a regular partner and senior undergraduate/postgraduate status (aOR = 1.83, 95% CI: 1.01–3.31); being vaccinated was additionally associated with female sex (aOR = 4.17, 95% CI 2.41–7.19) and medical major (aOR = 3.58, 95% CI: 2.15–5.95). title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) among adolescent girls and young women in a high HIV burden rural area of South Africa: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary cause of cervical cancer, with women living with HIV at increased risk of HPV infection and HPV-related disease. Data on HPV prevalence and genotype distribution among adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in rural South African settings remain limited. We estimated HPV prevalence, genotype distribution, and factors associated with HPV infection among AGYW in a high HIV prevalence district of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Methods This cross-sectional study was nested within the baseline survey of the Thetha Nami population-based trial among young people aged 15–30 years in rural uMkhanyakude District, KwaZulu-Natal. Survey participants were asked to provide dried blood spots for HIV testing and genital swabs for STI testing. For this study, we selected AGYW living with HIV with available vaginal swabs and a frequency-matched sample of AGYW without HIV. HPV genotyping was done using the HPV Direct Flow Chip Kit (Master Diagnostica, Spain). Genotype-specific HPV prevalence was described overall and by HIV status. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with HPV infection. Results Among 187 AGYW with valid HPV results, 90 (48.1%) were living with HIV. Overall HPV prevalence was 69.1% (95% confidence interval (CI) = 54.5–80.7%) and high-risk (hr)HPV prevalence was 57.3% (95%CI = 44.1–69.6%). HPV prevalence was higher among AGYW living with HIV than among AGYW without HIV (84.6% vs 64.6%, p = 0.02). HPV genotype distribution varied by HIV status: HPV35, HPV45 and HPV58 were the most prevalent hrHPV genotypes among AGYW living with HIV, vs HPV52, HPV56 and HPV31 among AGYW without HIV. No HPV16 or HPV18 infections were detected among participants who were age-eligible for the national HPV vaccination programme. Reported condomless sex (adjusted odds ratio (1) 2.23, 95%CI = 1.06–4.70) and the presence of another sexually transmitted infection (aOR = 4.30, 95%CI = 1.52–12.20) were associated with HPV infection. Conclusions AGYW in rural uMkhanyakude experience a high burden of hrHPV infection, especially those living with HIV. Regardless of HPV vaccination status not being confirmed, no HPV 16/18 was detected among vaccine-eligible AGYW. The higher prevalence of non-HPV16/18 hrHPV genotypes covered by the nonavalent vaccine highlights the potential value of vaccines with broader genotype coverage. These findings support expanding HPV screening and cervical cancer prevention programmes in high HIV prevalence settings.

title: How Does Health Literacy Shape Preventive Healthcare Decisions on Human Papillomavirus Vaccination?
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a preventive health intervention for persistent high-risk HPV infection that causes cervical and other HPV-associated cancers. Despite the availability of effective HPV vaccines and the integration of vaccination into national preventive strategies in many countries, uptake depends on factors beyond availability. Therefore, it is important to understand the influence of health literacy on preventive healthcare decisions about HPV vaccination. It is established that the link between health literacy and vaccination varies by group, age, and vaccine, and emerging work on vaccine literacy indicates that this link is not unidirectional. Evidence on HPV-specific health literacy is stronger among university students, showing a positive association between health literacy and knowledge of HPV, with knowledge scores varying between vaccinated and unvaccinated students, and health-literacy issues have been identified as both enablers of and barriers to college students’ vaccination decision-making. Based on the evidence, the paper argues that health literacy should be considered an integral part of HPV vaccination programmes, but not the cure-all for vaccine hesitancy. Health literacy affects vaccination as part of a wider health system alongside other factors such as provider recommendation, social influence, affordability, access, gender-based attitudes, culture, misinformation, and other health-system barriers. The paper also recommends a health-literacy–sensitive framework of accessible communication, trustworthy information, provider engagement, culturally sensitive information, digital health literacy, vaccination decision support, and easy vaccination access.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how health literacy influences preventive healthcare decisions regarding HPV vaccination, as HPV vaccination is a critical preventive health intervention for persistent high-risk HPV infection that leads to cervical and other HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on understanding the impact of health literacy on HPV vaccination decisions, particularly among university students, as evidence on HPV-specific health literacy is stronger in this group and shows a positive association between health literacy and knowledge of HPV.
analysis.methods: The study examined the relationship between health literacy and vaccination decision-making by analyzing knowledge scores among vaccinated and unvaccinated students, identifying health-literacy issues as both enablers and barriers to vaccination decisions.
analysis.main_results: The study found that health literacy is associated with knowledge of HPV, with knowledge scores varying between vaccinated and unvaccinated students, and that health-literacy issues have been identified as both enablers of and barriers to college students’ vaccination decision-making.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that health literacy affects vaccination as part of a wider health system, alongside other factors such as provider recommendation, social influence, affordability, access, gender-based attitudes, culture, misinformation, and other health-system barriers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that health literacy should be considered an integral part of HPV vaccination programs, but not the sole solution for vaccine hesitancy, highlighting the need for a health-literacy–sensitive framework to improve vaccination outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, and while it provides insights into the role of health literacy in HPV vaccination decisions, it does not offer detailed statistical analyses or broader population data, limiting the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how health literacy influences preventive healthcare decisions regarding HPV vaccination, emphasizing its role in shaping knowledge and vaccination behavior. The research highlights that health literacy is a significant factor in HPV vaccination decision-making, particularly among university students, where knowledge scores differ between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups. The authors argue that health literacy should be integrated into HPV vaccination programs but not viewed as a standalone solution for vaccine hesitancy. They recommend a health-literacy–sensitive framework that includes accessible communication, trustworthy information, provider engagement, and easy vaccination access. The study acknowledges that health literacy operates within a broader health system context, influenced by factors like provider recommendations, social influences, and cultural attitudes. However, the evidence is based on abstract-only data, which limits the depth of analysis and the strength of the conclusions.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how health literacy influences preventive healthcare decisions regarding HPV vaccination, as HPV vaccination is a critical preventive health intervention for persistent high-risk HPV infection that leads to cervical and other HPV-associated cancers.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study focused on understanding the impact of health literacy on HPV vaccination decisions, particularly among university students, as evidence on HPV-specific health literacy is stronger in this group and shows a positive association between health literacy and knowledge of HPV.
elements_en.methods: The study examined the relationship between health literacy and vaccination decision-making by analyzing knowledge scores among vaccinated and unvaccinated students, identifying health-literacy issues as both enablers and barriers to vaccination decisions.
elements_en.main_results: The study found that health literacy is associated with knowledge of HPV, with knowledge scores varying between vaccinated and unvaccinated students, and that health-literacy issues have been identified as both enablers of and barriers to college students’ vaccination decision-making.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that health literacy affects vaccination as part of a wider health system, alongside other factors such as provider recommendation, social influence, affordability, access, gender-based attitudes, culture, misinformation, and other health-system barriers.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that health literacy should be considered an integral part of HPV vaccination programs, but not the sole solution for vaccine hesitancy, highlighting the need for a health-literacy–sensitive framework to improve vaccination outcomes.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, and while it provides insights into the role of health literacy in HPV vaccination decisions, it does not offer detailed statistical analyses or broader population data, limiting the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨健康素养如何影响与HPV疫苗相关的预防性医疗决策,因为HPV疫苗是针对持续高危型HPV感染的关键预防性医疗干预措施,该感染会导致宫颈癌及其他HPV相关癌症。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究聚焦于理解健康素养对HPV疫苗决策的影响,特别是针对大学生群体,因为在此群体中有关HPV特异性健康素养的证据更为充分,并显示出健康素养与HPV知识之间的正向关联。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究通过分析接种疫苗和未接种疫苗学生的知识得分,探讨健康素养与HPV疫苗决策之间的关系,识别健康素养问题作为HPV疫苗决策的促进因素和阻碍因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 本研究发现,健康素养与HPV知识相关,接种疫苗和未接种疫苗学生之间的知识得分存在差异,且健康素养问题被识别为大学生HPV疫苗决策的促进因素和阻碍因素。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,健康素养影响HPV疫苗决策,是更广泛医疗体系的一部分,与其他因素如医生建议、社会影响、经济负担、可及性、基于性别态度、文化、错误信息及其他医疗体系障碍共同作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,健康素养应被视为HPV疫苗项目的重要组成部分,但不应是解决疫苗犹豫的唯一解决方案,强调了建立关注健康素养的框架以改善HPV疫苗结果的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于摘要内容,虽然提供了关于健康素养在HPV疫苗决策中作用的见解,但并未提供详细的统计分析或更广泛的人群数据,这限制了证据的强度。

title_zh: 健康素养如何影响人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)预防性医疗决策?
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a preventive health intervention for persistent high-risk HPV infection that causes cervical and other HPV-associated cancers. Despite the availability of effective HPV vaccines and the integration of vaccination into national preventive strategies in many countries, uptake depends on factors beyond availability. Therefore, it is important to understand the influence of health literacy on preventive healthcare decisions about HPV vaccination. It is established that the link between health literacy and vaccination varies by group, age, and vaccine, and emerging work on vaccine literacy indicates that this link is not unidirectional. Evidence on HPV-specific health literacy is stronger among university students, showing a positive association between health literacy and knowledge of HPV, with knowledge scores varying between vaccinated and unvaccinated students, and health-literacy issues have been identified as both enablers of and barriers to college students’ vaccination decision-making. Based on the evidence, the paper argues that health literacy should be considered an integral part of HPV vaccination programmes, but not the cure-all for vaccine hesitancy. Health literacy affects vaccination as part of a wider health system alongside other factors such as provider recommendation, social influence, affordability, access, gender-based attitudes, culture, misinformation, and other health-system barriers. The paper also recommends a health-literacy–sensitive framework of accessible communication, trustworthy information, provider engagement, culturally sensitive information, digital health literacy, vaccination decision support, and easy vaccination access.
abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是一种针对持续高危型HPV感染的预防性医疗干预措施,该感染会导致宫颈癌及其他HPV相关癌症。尽管已有有效的HPV疫苗,并且在许多国家已将HPV疫苗纳入国家预防战略,但疫苗接种率仍取决于除可获得性之外的其他因素。因此,理解健康素养对HPV疫苗预防性医疗决策的影响非常重要。已有研究表明,健康素养与HPV疫苗之间的关系因群体、年龄和疫苗类型而异,而关于疫苗相关健康素养的新兴研究则表明,这种关系并非单向。在大学生群体中,有关HPV特异性健康素养的证据更为充分,显示出健康素养与HPV知识之间存在正向关联,且接种疫苗的学生与未接种的学生在知识得分上存在差异。研究还指出,健康素养问题既是大学生HPV疫苗决策的促进因素,也是阻碍因素。基于现有证据,本文认为健康素养应被视为HPV疫苗项目的重要组成部分,但不应被视为解决疫苗犹豫的万能钥匙。健康素养影响HPV疫苗决策,是更广泛医疗体系的一部分,与其他因素如医生建议、社会影响、经济负担、可及性、基于性别态度、文化、错误信息及其他医疗体系障碍共同作用。本文还建议采用一种关注健康素养的框架,包括可访问的沟通方式、可信赖的信息、医生参与、文化敏感的信息、数字健康素养、HPV疫苗决策支持以及便捷的HPV疫苗获取途径。

title: Sociodemographic correlates of human papilloma virus (HPV) and cervical cancer knowledge among Saudi women
abstract: Human papilloma virus (HPV) is one of the most frequent sexually transmitted viruses globally, with serious clinical consequences, such as cervical cancer. This study aims to evaluate knowledge and awareness of, and attitudes and beliefs towards, HPV and vaccines for it among women from several Saudi Arabian regions. A cross-sectional descriptive study was carried out among Saudi Arabian women. Data were collected from December 9, 2024, to May 9, 2025, via an online survey including women’s demographics, knowledge, awareness, attitudes, and beliefs regarding HPV and vaccination against it. An overall of 627 women took part in the study. The majority of the population (32.1%) is aged from 36 to 45 years. In total, 47.4% of the participants have an adequate level of knowledge of HPV, 51.5% know that it is sexually transmitted, and 41.3% know that it can cause cervical cancer. The main information sources were the Ministry of Health and social media. Around 66.7% of the participants believed that the HPV vaccine is not safe. Marital status, religion, and educational status were demonstrably associated with overall knowledge and awareness of HPV and a vaccine for it. Age, marital status, children, region, education level, and occupation were significantly associated with beliefs concerning HPV. This study reported a gap in awareness and knowledge of cervical cancer and HPV; risk and HPV vaccination complications were found to be barriers to vaccine acceptance.

abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是全球最常见的一种性传播病毒之一,具有严重的临床后果,例如宫颈癌。本研究旨在评估沙特女性对HPV和疫苗的知识、意识、态度和信念。研究于2024年12月9日至2025年5月9日间在沙特阿拉伯多个地区进行,采用横断面描述性研究设计,通过在线调查收集数据,包括女性的人口学特征、对HPV和疫苗接种的知识、意识、态度和信念。共有627名女性参与了本研究。大多数参与者(32.1%)年龄在36至45岁之间。总体而言,47.4%的参与者对HPV有充分的知识,51.5%知道其为性传播病毒,41.3%知道其可导致宫颈癌。主要的信息来源是卫生部和社会媒体。约66.7%的参与者认为HPV 疫苗不安全。婚姻状况、宗教信仰和教育水平与HPV的整体知识和意识以及对疫苗的认知显著相关。年龄、婚姻状况、子女数量、地区、教育水平和职业与对HPV的态度信念显著相关。本研究指出在HPV和宫颈癌的知识和意识方面存在差距,发现对疫苗接种并发症的风险担忧是接受疫苗的障碍。

title: Systematic Review of Treatment Outcomes and Recurrence of Anogenital Warts in Patients Living With HIV
abstract: ABSTRACT Anogenital warts are common manifestations of human papillomavirus infection and remain challenging in people living with HIV because treatment response may be incomplete and recurrence may follow apparent clearance. This systematic review evaluated treatment outcomes and recurrence of anogenital warts in people living with HIV, including factors associated with therapeutic response. This study used a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PICOFramework. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for studies published from 2016 to 2026. Original studies reporting treatment outcomes in people living with HIV were eligible. Data were extracted and synthesized narratively. From 1,056 identified records, 10 studies were included. Treatments comprised topical, chemical, ablative, surgical, and combination approaches. Responses ranged from complete clearance to partial response and persistent disease. Recurrence varied substantially across studies and follow-up periods. In one cohort, all patients achieved primary clearance at three months, whereas cumulative recurrence reached 49.5% during follow-up extending to 10 years. Another long-term cohort reported recurrence in 60% of patients. HIV-related immune measures and lesion characteristics showed inconsistent associations with treatment outcomes. Treatment success in people living with HIV should be assessed beyond initial wart clearance. This review supports a response–durability framework distinguishing complete or partial response, persistent disease, and recurrence after documented clearance. Standardized reporting may strengthen future comparative research and evidence-based therapeutic strategies. Keywords: Condylomata Acuminata, HIV Infections, Treatment Outcome, Recurrence.

analysis.scope_and_question: Anogenital warts are common manifestations of human papillomavirus infection and remain challenging in people living with HIV because treatment response may be incomplete and recurrence may follow apparent clearance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review evaluated treatment outcomes and recurrence of anogenital warts in people living with HIV, including factors associated with therapeutic response. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for studies published from 2016 to 2026. Original studies reporting treatment outcomes in people living with HIV were eligible. Data were extracted and synthesized narratively.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: This study used a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PICOC framework. Treatments comprised topical, chemical, ablative, surgical, and combination approaches. Responses ranged from complete clearance to partial response and persistent disease. Recurrence varied substantially across studies and follow-up periods. In one cohort, all patients achieved primary clearance at three months, whereas cumulative recurrence reached 49.5% during follow-up extending to 10 years. Another long-term cohort reported recurrence in 60% of patients. HIV-related immune measures and lesion characteristics showed inconsistent associations with treatment outcomes. Treatment success in people living with HIV should be assessed beyond initial wart clearance.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Heterogeneity in treatment approaches and follow-up periods led to substantial variability in recurrence rates. Inconsistent associations between HIV-related immune measures and lesion characteristics with treatment outcomes highlight the need for further research. Missing data on long-term outcomes and standardized reporting methods limit the ability to draw definitive conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on identifying biomarkers that predict treatment response and recurrence in people living with HIV. Standardized reporting of treatment outcomes and follow-up periods is essential for comparative studies and evidence-based therapeutic strategies. Clinicians should consider a response–durability framework when evaluating treatment success in people living with HIV.

analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review evaluated treatment outcomes and recurrence of anogenital warts in people living with HIV, including factors associated with therapeutic response. Data were extracted and synthesized narratively.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: This study used a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PICOC framework. source_body_en: ABSTRACT Anogenital warts are common manifestations of human papillomavirus infection and remain challenging in people living with HIV because treatment response may be incomplete and recurrence may follow apparent clearance. title: Impact of HPV vaccination on high-risk HPV prevalence in 25-29-year-old women attending cervical screening in England 2016-2025
abstract: Background: In England, a national school-based human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme was introduced in September 2008. Routine vaccination against HPV16/18 is offered to girls aged 12-13 and a 'catch-up' offer ran for girls aged 14-18 during the programme's first two years. Methods: Data from 19,407 women aged 25-29yrs attending cervical screening across England 2016-2025 were collected and residual samples from 4,837 high-risk (HR) HPV-screening-positive women were genotyped to monitor type-specific HR-HPV prevalence and evaluate vaccination impact. Results: Type-specific HR-HPV results were available for 3,683 HR-HPV-screen-positive samples. Estimated age-adjusted prevalence of HPV16 and HPV18 was 91% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 87-94%) and 84% (95%CI: 65-93%) lower respectively among routine-eligible women than vaccination-ineligible women. Large declines were also observed for HPV31 (85% [95%CI: 72-92%]) and HPV45 (84% [95%CI: 73-90%]) but not for other HR-HPV types. Among 618 women with cytological abnormalities, HPV16/18 was present in samples from 53.9% (95%CI: 34.8-73.1%) of vaccination-ineligible, 18.1% (95%CI: 13.5-22.7%) of catch-up-eligible, and 6.5% (95%CI: 3.6-9.3%) of routine-eligible women. Conclusions: The early years of the HPV vaccination programme in England conferred strong protection against HPV16, 18, 31 and 45, and dramatically changed the target remaining for screening strategies to detect and reduce cervical disease.

Estimated age-adjusted prevalence of HPV16 and HPV18 was 91% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 87-94%) and 84% (95%CI: 65-93%) lower respectively among routine-eligible women than vaccination-ineligible women. Large declines were also observed for HPV31 (85% [95%CI: 72-92%]) and HPV45 (84% [95%CI: 73-90%]) but not for other HR-HPV types. Conclusions: The early years of the HPV vaccination programme in England conferred strong protection against HPV16, 18, 31 and 45, and dramatically changed the target remaining for screening strategies to detect and reduce cervical disease.

Methods: Data from 19,407 women aged 25-29yrs attending cervical screening across England 2016-2025 were collected and residual samples from 4,837 high-risk (HR) HPV-screening-positive women were genotyped to monitor type-specific HR-HPV prevalence and evaluate vaccination impact. Results: Type-specific HR-HPV results were available for 3,683 HR-HPV-screen-positive samples. Estimated age-adjusted prevalence of HPV16 and HPV18 was 91% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 87-94%) and 84% (95%CI: 65-93%) lower respectively among routine-eligible women than vaccination-ineligible women. Large declines were also observed for HPV31 (85% [95%CI: 72-92%]) and HPV45 (84% [95%CI: 73-90%]) but not for other HR-HPV types. Among 618 women with cytological abnormalities, HPV16/18 was present in samples from 53.9% (95%CI: 34.8-73.1%) of vaccination-ineligible, 18.1% (95%CI: 13.5-22.7%) of catch-up-eligible, and 6.5% (95%CI: 3.6-9.3%) of routine-eligible women. Conclusions: The early years of the HPV vaccination programme in England conferred strong protection against HPV16, 18, 31 and 45, and dramatically changed the target remaining for screening strategies to detect and reduce cervical disease.
title_original: Impact of HPV vaccination on high-risk HPV prevalence in 25-29-year-old women attending cervical screening in England 2016-2025

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of the HPV vaccination programme in England on high-risk HPV prevalence among 25-29-year-old women attending cervical screening between 2016 and 2025. It reports that the programme significantly reduced the prevalence of HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, and HPV45, with the largest declines observed for HPV16 and HPV18. Among women with cytological abnormalities, HPV16/18 prevalence was notably lower in routine-eligible women compared to vaccination-ineligible and catch-up-eligible groups. These findings highlight the effectiveness of HPV vaccination in reducing specific high-risk HPV types, which has important implications for cervical cancer screening strategies. However, the study relies on residual samples and lacks detailed statistical analyses, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

abstract_zh: 背景:在英格兰,一项基于学校的全国性 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗接种 计划于2008年9月启动。该计划为12-13岁的女孩提供常规 疫苗接种 针对HPV16/18,并在计划的前两年为14-18岁的女孩提供‘补种’机会。方法:收集了2016年至2025年间英格兰接受宫颈筛查的19,407名25-29岁女性的数据,并对其中4,837名高危型(HR)HPV筛查阳性的女性的残留样本进行基因分型,以监测特定高危型HPV的患病率并评估疫苗接种计划的影响。结果:共有3,683名HR-HPV筛查阳性的样本获得了特定高危型HPV的检测结果。与疫苗接种不符合条件的女性相比,常规符合条件的女性中HPV16和HPV18的年龄调整后患病率分别降低了91%(95%置信区间[CI]: 87-94%)和84%(95%CI: 65-93%)。此外,HPV31和HPV45也观察到显著下降(分别为85% [95%CI: 72-92%] 和84% [95%CI: 73-90%]),但其他高危型HPV未见明显下降。在618名有细胞学异常的女性中,HPV16/18分别在疫苗接种不符合条件的女性(53.9% [95%CI: 34.8-73.1%])、补种符合条件的女性(18.1% [95%CI: 13.5-22.7%])和常规符合条件的女性(6.5% [95%CI: 3.6-9.3%])的样本中被检测到。结论:英格兰HPV 疫苗接种 计划的早期阶段对HPV16、18、31和45提供了显著的保护作用,并极大地改变了宫颈疾病筛查策略的目标剩余。

title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Infection-Associated Epithelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition: Implication in Tumorigenesis and Pathogenesis of HPV-Positive Cancers
abstract: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a programmed and reversible process that allows epithelial cells to temporarily acquire a mesenchymal cell phenotype with increased migratory and invasive capacity. Analogous phenotypic modulation can also occur in carcinoma cells, which, after undergoing EMT, exhibit cancer stem cell-like properties and actively migrate, leading to tumor invasion and metastasis spread. This review focuses on the molecular crosstalk between human papillomavirus (HPV) and EMT, which occurs in HPV-infected human epithelium and in HPV-positive cancers of different location (cervical, head and neck, colorectal, lung and others). The main questions addressed here are: (i) how HPV-driven EMT contributes to the malignant transformation of HPV-infected epithelial cells, (ii) what mechanistic links exist between the HPV positivity and EMT in human cancers, and (iii) how EMT in various HPV-positive human tumors influences their pathogenesis, treatment modalities and outcomes. In this context, the relationship between HPV infection and EMT program is considered as a complex multicomponent mechanism triggered by exogenous and endogenous stimuli and involving specific ligand-receptor interactions, membrane channels, transcription factors, signaling pathways, epigenetic regulators etc. The present review also discusses some of the potential applications of EMT-related biomarkers and molecular targets in the prevention, prediction and treatment of HPV-induced cancers.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in HPV infection and its implications for the development of HPV-positive cancers. It highlights the molecular interactions between HPV and EMT, emphasizing how EMT contributes to tumor invasion and metastasis. The review also addresses the mechanisms linking HPV positivity to EMT in various cancers and discusses the potential of EMT-related biomarkers for cancer prevention, prediction, and treatment. The focus is on HPV types and their association with specific diseases, such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cancers, while excluding non-target viruses unless explicitly related to the target.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点探讨人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)与上皮-间质转化(EMT)之间的分子互作,这种互作发生在HPV感染的人类上皮组织以及不同部位的HPV阳性肿瘤(如宫颈癌、头颈癌、结直肠癌、肺癌等)中。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 综述讨论了HPV感染与EMT程序之间的关系,作为一种由外源性和内源性刺激触发的复杂多组分机制,涉及特定的配体-受体相互作用、膜通道、转录因子、信号通路、表观遗传调控因子等。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 上皮-间质转化(EMT)是一种程序化且可逆的过程,使上皮细胞暂时获得间质细胞表型,从而增强其迁移和侵袭能力。类似的现象调节也可以发生在癌细胞中,这些癌细胞在经历EMT后表现出类似癌症干细胞的特性,并主动迁移,导致肿瘤侵袭和转移扩散。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本文主要讨论以下问题:(i)HPV驱动的EMT如何促进HPV感染上皮细胞的恶性转化;(ii)HPV阳性与EMT之间存在哪些机制性联系;(iii)不同HPV阳性肿瘤中的EMT如何影响其治疗、预后模式和结果。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本综述还讨论了与EMT相关的生物标志物和分子靶点在预防、预测和治疗HPV诱导的癌症中的潜在应用。

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染相关上皮-间质转化:在肿瘤发生及HPV阳性肿瘤治疗中的意义
source_body_en: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a programmed and reversible process that allows epithelial cells to temporarily acquire a mesenchymal cell phenotype with increased migratory and invasive capacity. Analogous phenotypic modulation can also occur in carcinoma cells, which, after undergoing EMT, exhibit cancer stem cell-like properties and actively migrate, leading to tumor invasion and metastasis spread. This review focuses on the molecular crosstalk between human papillomavirus (HPV) and EMT, which occurs in HPV-infected human epithelium and in HPV-positive cancers of different location (cervical, head and neck, colorectal, lung and others). The main questions addressed here are: (i) how HPV-driven EMT contributes to the malignant transformation of HPV-infected epithelial cells, (ii) what mechanistic links exist between the HPV positivity and EMT in human cancers, and (iii) how EMT in various HPV-positive human tumors influences their pathogenesis, treatment modalities and outcomes. In this context, the relationship between HPV infection and EMT program is considered as a complex multicomponent mechanism triggered by exogenous and endogenous stimuli and involving specific ligand-receptor interactions, membrane channels, transcription factors, signaling pathways, epigenetic regulators etc. The present review also discusses some of the potential applications of EMT-related biomarkers and molecular targets in the prevention, prediction and treatment of HPV-induced cancers.
abstract_zh: 上皮-间质转化(EMT)是一种程序化且可逆的过程,使上皮细胞暂时获得间质细胞表型,从而增强其迁移和侵袭能力。类似的现象调节也可以发生在癌细胞中,这些癌细胞在经历EMT后表现出类似癌症干细胞的特性,并主动迁移,导致肿瘤侵袭和转移扩散。本综述重点探讨人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)与EMT之间的分子互作,这种互作发生在HPV感染的人类上皮组织以及不同部位的HPV阳性肿瘤(如宫颈癌、头颈癌、结直肠癌、肺癌等)中。本文主要讨论以下问题:(i)HPV驱动的EMT如何促进HPV感染上皮细胞的恶性转化;(ii)HPV阳性与EMT之间存在哪些机制性联系;(iii)不同HPV阳性肿瘤中的EMT如何影响其治疗、预后模式和结果。在此背景下,HPV感染与EMT程序之间的关系被视为一种由外源性和内源性刺激触发的复杂多组分机制,涉及特定的配体-受体相互作用、膜通道、转录因子、信号通路、表观遗传调控因子等。本综述还讨论了与EMT相关的生物标志物和分子靶点在预防、预测和治疗HPV诱导的癌症中的潜在应用。

title: Human Papillomavirus Infection in Patients With VaIN and Vaginal Cancer: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Vaginal cancer is a rare malignancy, and the research on it is not comprehensive yet. To explore the characteristics of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) and vaginal cancer. METHODS: This study included patients who underwent colposcopy and biopsy of suspected sites at the Second Hospital of Shanxi Medical University from January 2014 to December 2023 due to abnormal cytology results and/or positive HPV test. Those diagnosed with benign inflammatory reaction of the vagina (ie, vaginitis), VaIN and vaginal cancer according to histologic results were selected as the study objects. Clinical data such as age, menopause, clinical manifestations and previous screening history were collected. We aimed to analyze the distribution and characteristics of HPV in VaIN and vaginal cancer patients. RESULTS: A total of 5,180 patients were included in this study. Of the total, 2,739 patients had VaIN1, 641 had VaIN2/3, and 251 had vaginal cancer. There were 235 patients with vaginal squamous cell carcinoma (VaSCC) and 16 patients with vaginal adenocarcinoma. A total of 4,548 patients were infected with HPV. The HPV positive rate was 95.5% in VaIN2/3, 86.0% in VaSCC and 43.8% in adenocarcinoma of the vagina. The most common 5 HPV types were HPV16, 52, 58, 53, and 18. The positive rate of HPV18 in the adenocarcinoma of the vagina was the highest. CONCLUSION: HPV16, 52, 58, 53, and 18 are the predominant genotypes in VaIN and vaginal cancer in Shanxi, China. HPV testing provides additional benefits for the detection of vaginal lesions during cervical cancer screening. Active HPV vaccination may help reduce the burden of these lesions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the characteristics of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) and vaginal cancer, addressing the need for comprehensive research on vaginal cancer.

title: Comparison of Colorimetric LAMP and PCR for High-risk HPV Detection: Implications for Cervical Cancer Screening.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer, primarily caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, is commonly detected using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based assays. However, these methods are time-consuming and require specialized instrumentation. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay as a rapid alternative for HPV detection compared with conventional PCR testing. METHODS: This study included 933 nonpregnant women aged ≥19 years who underwent HPV testing for cervical cancer screening or follow-up. The HPV panel included 14 high-risk types (16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68). Cervical swab samples underwent nucleic acid extraction followed by LAMP amplification using type-specific primers. Reactions were performed at 63 °C for 35 minutes, and results were interpreted colorimetrically (blue for positive, purple for negative). RESULTS: Compared with PCR, the LAMP assay showed a sensitivity of 97.8% (95% CI: 94.4-100.0) for HPV types 16 and 18 and 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8-100.0) for the remaining high-risk types. Specificity across all types was 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8-100.0). The overall diagnostic accuracy was 99.5% (95% CI: 99.0-100.0). When all 14 HPV types were analyzed collectively, clinical sensitivity and specificity were 99.4% and 100.0%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The LAMP assay provides a rapid, simple, and accurate method for HPV detection and may serve as a useful point-of-care screening tool, particularly in resource-limited settings.

title_zh: 色谱LAMP与PCR在高危型HPV检测中的比较:对宫颈癌筛查的启示。
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer, primarily caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, is commonly detected using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based assays. However, these methods are time-consuming and require specialized instrumentation. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay as a rapid alternative for HPV detection compared with conventional PCR testing. METHODS: This study included 933 nonpregnant women aged ≥19 years who underwent HPV testing for cervical cancer screening or follow-up. The HPV panel included 14 high-risk types (16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68). Cervical swab samples underwent nucleic acid extraction followed by LAMP amplification using type-specific primers. Reactions were performed at 63 °C for 35 minutes, and results were interpreted colorimetrically (blue for positive, purple for negative). RESULTS: Compared with PCR, the LAMP assay showed a sensitivity of 97.8% (95% CI: 94.4-100.0) for HPV types 16 and 18 and 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8-100.0) for the remaining high-risk types. Specificity across all types was 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8-100.0). The overall diagnostic accuracy was 99.5% (95% CI: 99.0-100.0). When all 14 HPV types were analyzed collectively, clinical sensitivity and specificity were 99.4% and 100.0%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The LAMP assay provides a rapid, simple, and accurate method for HPV detection and may serve as a useful point-of-care screening tool, particularly in resource-limited settings.
abstract_zh: 目的:宫颈癌主要由人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒,HPV)感染引起,通常使用基于聚合酶链反应(PCR)的检测方法进行检测。然而,这些方法耗时且需要专门的仪器。本研究评估了环介导等温扩增(LAMP)检测方法作为快速替代方案在HPV检测中的诊断性能,并与传统PCR检测方法进行比较。方法:本研究纳入了933名≥19岁的非妊娠女性,她们接受了宫颈癌筛查或随访的HPV检测。HPV检测面板包括14种高危型(16、18、31、33、35、39、45、51、52、56、58、59、66和68型)。宫颈拭子样本经过核酸提取后,使用型特异性引物进行LAMP扩增。反应在63 °C下进行35分钟,结果通过颜色变化进行解读(蓝色表示阳性,紫色表示阴性)。结果:与PCR相比,LAMP检测方法对HPV 16和18型的敏感性为97.8%(95% CI:94.4-100.0),对其他高危型的敏感性为100.0%(95% CI:98.8-100.0)。所有类型的特异性为100.0%(95% CI:98.8-100.0)。总体诊断准确度为99.5%(95% CI:99.0-100.0)。当对所有14种HPV类型进行整体分析时,临床敏感性和特异性分别为99.4%和100.0%。结论:LAMP检测方法为HPV检测提供了一种快速、简便且准确的方法,可能在资源有限的环境中作为有用的床边筛查工具。

title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the Human Papillomavirus Prevention Health Literacy Scale for College Students in Taiwan.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus associated with several types of cancer. Because college students are a high-risk group, understanding their health literacy with regard to HPV prevention is critical. However, no suitable measurement tools are currently available for this purpose. PURPOSE: In this study, an HPV Prevention Health Literacy Scale (HPV-HLS) was developed, and its reliability and validity were assessed. METHODS: A cross-sectional design was used, and the developed scale was validated on a sample of 372 college students from two universities in northern Taiwan and one university in central Taiwan. The initial scale comprised 49 items, developed from qualitative interviews and a literature review. After content validity assessment and item analysis, the scale was refined to 37 items. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted with 150 participants, followed by confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with 222 participants. Concurrent validity and internal consistency reliability were assessed. Data were collected from November 2021 to December 2022. RESULTS: The results of the EFA revealed a two-factor model accounted for 60.30% of the total variation, and those of the CFA demonstrated favorable goodness-of-fit indices (GFI = .81, CFI = .92, TLI = .91, RMSEA = .07, and SRMR = .02). Moreover, the average variance extracted (AVE) for the two factors were .56 and .64, respectively, with corresponding composite reliability (CR) values of .96 and .93, indicating excellent convergent validity. Notably, the AVE surpassed the squared product-moment correlation of the corresponding factors, affirming good discriminant validity. The final iteration of the HPV-HLS comprised 21 items with two subscales: comprehension and evaluation of general information and seeking information from health care professionals. Concurrent validity was found between the proposed scale and the Mandarin Multidimensional Health Literacy Questionnaire ( r = .68, p < .001). The HPV-HLS demonstrated good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .959). CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS FOR FUTURE PRACTICE: After rigorous psychometric testing, the newly developed HPV-HLS demonstrated excellent reliability and validity, establishing it as an objective tool for evaluating HPV prevention health literacy among college students. This HPV-HLS may be used by health care providers and educators to assess health literacy and evaluate the effectiveness of clinical interventions to prevent HPV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and validate a psychometric tool, the HPV Prevention Health Literacy Scale (HPV-HLS), to assess health literacy related to HPV prevention among college students in Taiwan. The research was conducted using a cross-sectional design with a sample of 372 students from three universities.
