title: Acceptability and preference of self-collected vaginal samples for human papillomavirus DNA testing compared with physician-collected Pap smear.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-collected vaginal sampling for human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing provides a promising alternative to physician-collected Pap smears, especially in low-resource settings. However, data on its acceptability and preferences among Filipino women remain limited. This study aimed to assess women's perceptions, experiences, willingness and preferences regarding self-collected vaginal sampling for HPV DNA testing compared with Pap smears. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 592 women. Participants underwent both physician-collected Pap smears and self-collected vaginal sampling for HPV DNA testing. Perceptions were measured using five-point Likert scale questionnaires before and after self-collection. Descriptive statistics were used, and paired and independent Wilcoxon tests were used to compare Likert responses. Willingness to undergo screening was analyzed with Cochran's Q and McNemar tests. Participants' reasons for their preferred screening method were categorized thematically and displayed in stacked bar charts. RESULTS: Self-collection was generally viewed as painless, not uncomfortable, non-embarrassing, and easy and convenient. Acceptability significantly increased after participants performed self-collection (P < 0.001 for pain and discomfort). Compared with Pap smears, self-collection was seen as less embarrassing (P < 0.001), but rated as less easy (P = 0.01) and less convenient (P = 0.004). Most participants preferred physician-administered screening (84.8%) due to trust in medical expertise, and confidence in the procedure's accuracy, safety and cleanliness. CONCLUSIONS: Self-collected vaginal sampling was highly acceptable, yet physician-collected screening remained the preferred method. Improving education, demonstrations, and support for self-collection may enhance the uptake of HPV DNA testing and broaden access to cervical cancer screening in the Philippines.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 自我采集阴道样本用于人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)DNA检测为医生采集的巴氏涂片提供了一种有前景的替代方案,特别是在资源匮乏的环境中。然而,关于菲律宾女性对其可接受性和偏好的数据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在592名女性中进行了一项横断面研究。参与者接受了医生采集的巴氏涂片和自我采集的阴道样本用于HPV DNA检测。
elements_zh.methods: 感知通过五点李克特量表问卷在自我采样前和后进行测量。使用描述性统计,并采用配对和独立样本威尔科克森检验来比较李克特量表的回答。接受筛查的意愿通过科克兰Q检验和麦克纳马检验进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 自我采集通常被认为无痛、不不适、不尴尬且容易和方便。参与者进行自我采集后,可接受性显著提高(疼痛和不适的P < 0.001)。与巴氏涂片相比,自我采集被认为更不尴尬(P < 0.001),但被认为更不便于操作(P = 0.01)和更不方便(P = 0.004)。大多数参与者由于对医疗专业知识的信任以及对程序准确性、安全性和清洁度的信心,更倾向于医生进行的筛查(84.8%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 自我采集阴道样本具有高度可接受性,但医生采集的筛查仍然是首选方法。通过改善自我采集的教育、演示和支持,可能提高HPV DNA检测的参与率,并扩大菲律宾宫颈癌筛查的可及性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能通过强调自我采样方法的教育和支持需求,为提高菲律宾HPV DNA检测的接受度并扩大筛查可及性提供策略依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于菲律宾的一个特定人群,未考虑长期依从性或结果。证据强度中等,因为其基于自我报告的感知和偏好。

title: Quercetin, an active component of Qiu's HuaShi decoction, suppresses glycolysis in cervical epithelial cells to reduce HPV infection via modulating the PRKACA/cAMP/PKA/CREB pathway.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is strongly associated with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) and poses a substantial threat to women's health. Qiu's HuaShi Decoction (QHD) exhibits potential in cervical cancer treatment, yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. METHODS: Network pharmacology was utilized to screen the core targets of QHD against HPV-associated cervical cancer. The anti-tumor effects of quercetin were evaluated through integrated in vivo and in vitro experiments. Immunofluorescence staining was applied to observe the status of HPV16 infection. Meanwhile, qRT-PCR and western blot were used to detect the mRNA and protein expression levels of HPV16 oncogenes E6 and E7. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used for in situ validation of protein expression in animal tissues. In addition, western blot was performed to quantify the protein levels of key molecules involved in the PRKACA/PKA/CREB axis and core glycolytic regulators. Furthermore, cAMP content, cellular glucose uptake, lactate production and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and oxygen consumption rate (OCR) were assessed by commercial kits. Additionally, PRKACA overexpression experiments were performed to dissect the regulatory role of PRKACA in quercetin-mediated effects. RESULTS: Network pharmacology analysis identified quercetin and PRKACA as the core targets of QHD for combating HPV-associated cervical cancer. Quercetin inhibited early HPV16 infection, downregulated HPV16 E6/E7 expression, and suppressed cell proliferation. Mechanistically, quercetin reduced intracellular cAMP levels, inactivated the cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling axis, and suppressed the expression of key glycolytic proteins. Consistently, quercetin suppressed glycolytic phenotypes, including reduced glucose uptake, lactate secretion, and ATP production, accompanied by decreased ECAR and restored OCR in cervical epithelial cells. These phenotypic effects were reversed by PRKACA overexpression. CONCLUSIONS: Quercetin exerts its anti-tumor effects against HPV-related cervical cancer by inhibiting PRKACA expression to disrupt cAMP/PKA/CREB/glycolysis signaling axis, providing a molecular basis for the clinical application of QHD.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects

title_zh: 槲皮素,邱华石汤剂的活性成分,通过调控PRKACA/cAMP/PKA/CREB通路抑制宫颈上皮细胞糖酵解以减少HPV感染。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is strongly associated with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) and poses a substantial threat to women's health. Qiu's HuaShi Decoction (QHD) exhibits potential in cervical cancer treatment, yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. METHODS: Network pharmacology was utilized to screen the core targets of QHD against HPV-associated cervical cancer. The anti-tumor effects of quercetin were evaluated through integrated in vivo and in vitro experiments. Immunofluorescence staining was applied to observe the status of HPV16 infection. Meanwhile, qRT-PCR and western blot were used to detect the mRNA and protein expression levels of HPV16 oncogenes E6 and E7. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used for in situ validation of protein expression in animal tissues. In addition, western blot was performed to quantify the protein levels of key molecules involved in the PRKACA/PKA/CREB axis and core glycolytic regulators. Furthermore, cAMP content, cellular glucose uptake, lactate production and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and oxygen consumption rate (OCR) were assessed by commercial kits. Additionally, PRKACA overexpression experiments were performed to dissect the regulatory role of PRKACA in quercetin-mediated effects. RESULTS: Network pharmacology analysis identified quercetin and PRKACA as the core targets of QHD for combating HPV-associated cervical cancer. Quercetin inhibited early HPV16 infection, downregulated HPV16 E6/E7 expression, and suppressed cell proliferation. Mechanistically, quercetin reduced intracellular cAMP levels, inactivated the cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling axis, and suppressed the expression of key glycolytic proteins. Consistently, quercetin suppressed glycolytic phenotypes, including reduced glucose uptake, lactate secretion, and ATP production, accompanied by decreased ECAR and restored OCR in cervical epithelial cells. These phenotypic effects were reversed by PRKACA overexpression. CONCLUSIONS: Quercetin exerts its anti-tumor effects against HPV-related cervical cancer by inhibiting PRKACA expression to disrupt cAMP/PKA/CREB/glycolysis signaling axis, providing a molecular basis for the clinical application of QHD.
abstract_zh: 背景:宫颈癌与高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的持续感染密切相关,并对女性健康构成重大威胁。邱华石汤剂(QHD)在宫颈癌 治疗中展现出潜在的治疗作用,但其作用机制尚不明确。方法:通过网络药理学筛选QHD针对HPV相关宫颈癌的核心靶点。通过整合体内和体外实验评估槲皮素的抗肿瘤效果。采用免疫荧光染色观察HPV16感染状态。同时,利用qRT-PCR和Western blot检测HPV16致癌基因E6和E7的mRNA和蛋白表达水平。免疫组织化学(IHC)用于动物组织中蛋白表达的原位验证。此外,通过Western blot定量分析PRKACA/PKA/CREB轴和核心糖酵解调节因子的关键分子蛋白水平。进一步,使用商业试剂盒评估cAMP含量、细胞葡萄糖摄取、乳酸产生以及细胞外酸化率(ECAR)和耗氧率(OCR)。此外,进行了PRKACA过表达实验以解析其在槲皮素介导效应中的调控作用。结果:网络药理学分析确定槲皮素和PRKACA为QHD对抗HPV相关宫颈癌的核心靶点。槲皮素抑制了早期HPV16感染,下调了HPV16 E6/E7的表达,并抑制了细胞增殖。机制上,槲皮素降低了细胞内cAMP水平,使cAMP/PKA/CREB信号轴失活,并抑制了关键糖酵解蛋白的表达。一致地,槲皮素抑制了糖酵解表型,包括葡萄糖摄取减少、乳酸分泌减少和ATP生成减少,同时伴随ECAR降低和OCR恢复。这些表型效应可通过PRKACA过表达逆转。结论:槲皮素通过抑制PRKACA表达来破坏cAMP/PKA/CREB/糖酵解信号轴,从而发挥其针对HPV相关宫颈癌的抗肿瘤作用,为QHD的临床应用提供了分子基础。

title: A study to assess the knowledge, perceived roles and training needs of school teachers regarding human papillomavirus vaccination programs in selected schools of Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India
abstract: Background: Cervical cancer is a critical global health challenge, with India bearing over 22% of worldwide mortality. School teachers are vital, trusted stakeholders who can mitigate vaccine hesitancy and champion adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) immunization. However, institutional frameworks rarely address teachers' internal educational deficits. This study evaluated the baseline health literacy, perceived roles, and training needs of school teachers in Dehradun, India. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 110 school teachers across selected government and private schools named shri guru ram rai (SGRR) public school, Government Primary School, Charan Haly Child School, Floridale School, Government Girls Inter College (GGIC), Prabhanand Children Academy, Government Inter College, and Shivalik Hills Academy in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India from Jan to June 2026 using convenience sampling. Data were gathered via self-structured, validated instruments capturing socio-demographics, knowledge, perceived roles, and training needs. An evidence-based HPV awareness pamphlet was distributed immediately following baseline assessments. Results: The cohort was predominantly female (90.9%) and lacked prior exposure to school health programs (96.4%) or HPV training (100.0%). Severe health literacy deficits were observed, with 77.3% of teachers demonstrating poor baseline knowledge. Institutional disconnect was high; 63.6% exhibited poor commitment regarding active responsibilities in vaccine promotion. Conversely, 81.8% indicated high training demands, with an exceptional overall scale mean of 4.68 out of 5.0. Notably, the highest demand (μ=4.80) was for structured educational materials (like pamphlets) to distribute during parent-teacher meetings. Conclusions: While educators possess critically low baseline clinical awareness and professional involvement regarding HPV, they demonstrate immense, proactive motivation for capacity building. Distributing targeted, evidence-based awareness pamphlets represents an affordable, highly scalable intervention to bridge institutional gaps, empower educators, and foster supportive school environments for adolescent immunization.
journal: International Journal of Reproduction, Contraception, Obstetrics and Gynecology

title_zh: 一项评估德里达尔恩市乌塔拉甘特邦印度选定学校中学校教师对人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种项目的知识、感知角色和培训需求的研究
source_body_en: Background: Cervical cancer is a critical global health challenge, with India bearing over 22% of worldwide mortality. School teachers are vital, trusted stakeholders who can mitigate vaccine hesitancy and champion adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) immunization. However, institutional frameworks rarely address teachers' internal educational deficits. This study evaluated the baseline health literacy, perceived roles, and training needs of school teachers in Dehradun, India. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 110 school teachers across selected government and private schools named shri guru ram rai (SGRR) public school, Government Primary School, Charan Haly Child School, Floridale School, Government Girls Inter College (GGIC), Prabhanand Children Academy, Government Inter College, and Shivalik Hills Academy in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India from Jan to June 2026 using convenience sampling. Data were gathered via self-structured, validated instruments capturing socio-demographics, knowledge, perceived roles, and training needs. An evidence-based HPV awareness pamphlet was distributed immediately following baseline assessments. Results: The cohort was predominantly female (90.9%) and lacked prior exposure to school health programs (96.4%) or HPV training (100.0%). Severe health literacy deficits were observed, with 77.3% of teachers demonstrating poor baseline knowledge. Institutional disconnect was high; 63.6% exhibited poor commitment regarding active responsibilities in vaccine promotion. Conversely, 81.8% indicated high training demands, with an exceptional overall scale mean of 4.68 out of 5.0. Notably, the highest demand (μ=4.80) was for structured educational materials (like pamphlets) to distribute during parent-teacher meetings. Conclusions: While educators possess critically low baseline clinical awareness and professional involvement regarding HPV, they demonstrate immense, proactive motivation for capacity building. Distributing targeted, evidence-based awareness pamphlets represents an affordable, highly scalable intervention to bridge institutional gaps, empower educators, and foster supportive school environments for adolescent immunization.
abstract_zh: 背景:宫颈癌是全球性的健康挑战,印度承担了全球死亡率的22%以上。学校教师是关键且值得信赖的利益相关者,能够缓解疫苗的犹豫态度并推动青少年人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗接种。然而,机构框架很少涉及教师内部的教育缺陷。本研究评估了印度德里达尔恩市选定学校中学校教师的基线健康素养、感知角色和培训需求。方法:采用描述性横断面研究设计,于2026年1月至6月期间,通过便利抽样方式在德里达尔恩市乌塔拉甘特邦选定的政府和私立学校(包括 shri guru ram rai(SGRR)公立学校、政府小学、Charan Haly儿童学校、Floridale学校、政府女子综合学院(GGIC)、Prabhanand儿童学院、政府综合学院和Shivalik Hills学院)中对110名学校教师进行调查。数据通过自设结构化、经过验证的工具收集,涵盖社会人口学、知识、感知角色和培训需求。在基线评估后立即分发基于证据的HPV意识传单。结果:队列研究中女性占主导地位(90.9%),且缺乏对学校健康项目(96.4%)或HPV培训(100.0%)的先前接触。观察到严重的健康素养缺陷,77.3%的教师表现出较差的基线知识水平。机构脱节现象严重,63.6%的教师在推动疫苗方面表现出较差的承诺。相反,81.8%的教师表示有较高的培训需求,整体量表均值达到4.68(满分5.0)。值得注意的是,最高需求(μ=4.80)是希望在家长教师会议上分发结构化的教育材料(如传单)。结论:尽管教育工作者在HPV方面的基线临床意识和专业参与度极低,但他们表现出巨大的、主动的能力建设意愿。分发有针对性的、基于证据的意识传单是一种经济实惠且高度可扩展的干预措施,有助于弥合机构间的差距,增强教育工作者的能力,并营造支持青少年疫苗接种的学校环境。

title: Human Papillomavirus-Associated Vulvar Intraepithelial Neoplasia in an Immunocompromised Patient—When Excisional Treatment Is Not Possible
abstract: Human papillomavirus-associated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (HPVa VIN) is a premalignant condition. Its main risk factors include human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, smoking, and immunodeficiency. Excisional treatment is preferred, but if contraindicated, topical imiquimod may be considered. The prognosis appears to be similar after these two treatments. Still, there are few studies in women living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) to draw a conclusion in this group. We present the case of a woman living with HIV and meeting diagnostic criteria for acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), with extensive, multifocal, and recurrent HPVa VIN. Due to anesthetic contraindications, we opted for topical imiquimod treatment, with good results, achieving a complete clinical response after 18 weeks of treatment. Two months later, a clinically suspected recurrence was detected, and imiquimod was reinitiated. Complete clinical resolution was again achieved after 20 weeks of treatment, and the patient started clinical surveillance every 3 months.

title: Digital Health Literacy and Parental Willingness for School-Based Human Papillomavirus Vaccination: The Importance of Online Information Searching Skill
abstract: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a highly effective primary prevention measure, with over 90% efficacy in preventing cervical cancer. This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination in Depok City, Indonesia. Data were collected via an online self-administered questionnaire completed by 208 parents. Despite a high overall willingness rate (88.9%), significant gaps remain between general vaccine awareness and detailed operational knowledge regarding dosage and timing. Using a cross-sectional design and multivariable logistic regression, the research identifies that insufficient information exposure is the primary barrier to vaccine acceptance (AOR: 0.06; 95%CI: 0.02 – 0.22). Notably, digital health literacy, specifically proficient online information-searching skills, emerged as a critical enabler of vaccination intent. Conversely, lower skills in self-generated digital content were associated with higher willingness, suggesting a correlation between passive digital engagement and program acceptance. These findings indicate that the success of the School Children’s Immunization Month (BIAS) depends on transitioning from one-way administrative announcements to interactive, literacy-based communication strategies. Strengthening parental digital competencies and fostering structured school-based dialogues are essential to bridging the knowledge-action gap. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to evaluate the long-term impact of digital literacy interventions on actual vaccine uptake across diverse Indonesian contexts.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination in Depok City, Indonesia, addressing the knowledge gap in vaccine awareness and operational details.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Depok City, Indonesia, involving 208 parents, to examine the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination.
analysis.methods: Data were collected via an online self-administered questionnaire, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify barriers to vaccine acceptance.
analysis.main_results: Despite a high overall willingness rate (88.9%), significant gaps exist between general vaccine awareness and detailed operational knowledge regarding dosage and timing. Insufficient information exposure was identified as the primary barrier to vaccine acceptance (AOR: 0.06; 95%CI: 0.02 – 0.22).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that digital health literacy, specifically proficient online information-searching skills, emerged as a critical enabler of vaccination intent, while lower skills in self-generated digital content were associated with higher willingness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening parental digital competencies and fostering structured school-based dialogues are essential to bridge the knowledge-action gap and improve vaccine uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit the generalizability of the findings. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to evaluate the long-term impact of digital literacy interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study in Depok City, Indonesia, found that digital health literacy, particularly online information-searching skills, is crucial for parental willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination. Despite high overall willingness, gaps in vaccine awareness and operational knowledge were identified, with insufficient information exposure being the primary barrier.

analysis_en.methods: Data were collected via an online self-administered questionnaire, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify barriers to vaccine acceptance.

title_zh: 数字健康素养与家长对学校接种人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种的意愿:在线信息检索技能的重要性
source_body_en: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a highly effective primary prevention measure, with over 90% efficacy in preventing cervical cancer. This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination in Depok City, Indonesia. Data were collected via an online self-administered questionnaire completed by 208 parents. Despite a high overall willingness rate (88.9%), significant gaps remain between general vaccine awareness and detailed operational knowledge regarding dosage and timing. Using a cross-sectional design and multivariable logistic regression, the research identifies that insufficient information exposure is the primary barrier to vaccine acceptance (AOR: 0.06; 95%CI: 0.02 – 0.22). Notably, digital health literacy, specifically proficient online information-searching skills, emerged as a critical enabler of vaccination intent. Conversely, lower skills in self-generated digital content were associated with higher willingness, suggesting a correlation between passive digital engagement and program acceptance. These findings indicate that the success of the School Children’s Immunization Month (BIAS) depends on transitioning from one-way administrative announcements to interactive, literacy-based communication strategies. Strengthening parental digital competencies and fostering structured school-based dialogues are essential to bridging the knowledge-action gap. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to evaluate the long-term impact of digital literacy interventions on actual vaccine uptake across diverse Indonesian contexts.
abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒)疫苗接种是一种高度有效的初级预防措施,可预防宫颈癌,其有效性超过90%。本横断面研究探讨了家长健康素养与接受学校接种HPV 疫苗接种意愿之间的关系,研究地点为印度尼西亚德波克市。数据通过在线自填式问卷收集,共有208名家长参与。尽管总体意愿率较高(88.9%),但家长对疫苗的一般认知与具体操作知识(如剂量和时间)之间仍存在显著差距。采用横断面设计和多变量逻辑回归分析,研究发现信息暴露不足是疫苗接受的主要障碍(AOR: 0.06;95%CI: 0.02 – 0.22)。值得注意的是,数字健康素养,特别是熟练的在线信息检索技能,被发现是疫苗接种意愿的关键促进因素。相反,较低的自生成数字内容技能则与较高的意愿相关,表明被动的数字参与与项目接受之间存在相关性。这些发现表明,学校儿童免疫月(BIAS)的成功取决于从单向行政公告向互动、基于素养的沟通策略转变。加强家长的数字能力并促进结构化的学校对话对于弥合知识与行动之间的差距至关重要。未来的研究应采用纵向设计,以评估数字素养干预措施在不同印尼背景下的长期影响对实际疫苗接种率的影响。

title: Knowledge and Attitudes towards Human Papillomavirus and HPV vaccination among girls aged 9-14 years in Lira City West, Northern Uganda: A cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the necessary cause of nearly all cervical cancers and remains an important public-health problem, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Vaccination before exposure to HPV is an effective primary prevention strategy. This study assessed knowledge of HPV and HPV vaccination and attitudes towards HPV vaccination among girls aged 9–14 years attending selected primary schools in Lira City West Division, Northern Uganda. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among 398 girls aged 9–14 years from three high-enrolment primary schools. Participants were stratified by school and class and selected systematically within strata. Data were collected using an interviewer-administered structured questionnaire in English or Leb Lango. Sociodemographic characteristics, individual knowledge items and five-point Likert attitude items were analysed descriptively using frequencies and percentages in IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Results: Only 26.4% of participants had heard of HPV and 15.6% identified HPV as a virus associated with cervical cancer. When asked about transmission, 65.8% selected sexual contact and 14.6% selected skin-to-skin contact. Awareness of the HPV vaccine was higher, with 76.9% having heard of it and 86.7% indicating that it can prevent cervical cancer. Favourable attitudes were common: 77.9% intended to receive the vaccine, 79.4% perceived it as safe, 78.6% considered vaccination important and 77.9% would recommend it to friends. Parents or guardians influenced vaccination views among 75.1% of participants. However, 95.0% disagreed or strongly disagreed that sufficient HPV-vaccine information was available to them. Conclusion: Girls in the selected schools were generally receptive to HPV vaccination but had limited understanding of HPV infection and its relationship with cervical cancer. The findings show a mismatch between relatively high vaccine awareness and favourable attitudes, and limited HPV knowledge alongside perceived insufficiency of information. School-based vaccination should be accompanied by repeated, age-appropriate education involving girls, parents and health workers.

The findings show a mismatch between relatively high vaccine awareness and favourable attitudes, and limited HPV knowledge alongside perceived insufficiency of information. School-based vaccination should be accompanied by repeated, age-appropriate education involving girls, parents and health workers.
abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是几乎所有宫颈癌的必要病因,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家,仍然是重要的公共卫生问题。在接触HPV之前接种疫苗接种是一种有效的初级预防策略。本研究评估了9–14岁女孩对HPV及其疫苗接种的知识和态度,这些女孩来自乌干达北部Lira市西区的三所高入学率的初级学校。方法:在三所高入学率初级学校中,对398名9–14岁女孩进行了定量横断面研究。参与者按学校和班级进行分层,并在分层内系统抽样。数据通过英语或Leb Lango的访谈式结构化问卷收集,并使用IBM SPSS Statistics版本27进行描述性分析,包括社会人口学特征、知识项目和五点李克特量表态度项目。结果:只有26.4%的参与者听说过HPV,其中15.6%将HPV识别为与宫颈癌相关的病毒。当被问及传播的传播途径时,65.8%的参与者选择了性接触,14.6%选择了皮肤接触。对于HPV 疫苗的知晓率更高,76.9%的参与者听说过它,86.7%的参与者认为它可以预防宫颈癌。积极的态度较为普遍:77.9%的参与者表示有意接种疫苗,79.4%的参与者认为其安全,78.6%的参与者认为疫苗接种重要,77.9%的参与者会向朋友推荐它。75.1%的参与者表示父母或监护人影响了他们对疫苗接种的看法。然而,95.0%的参与者不同意或强烈不同意他们获得了足够的HPV-疫苗信息。结论:所选学校中的女孩总体上对HPV 疫苗接种持开放态度,但对HPV感染及其与宫颈癌的关系了解有限。研究结果表明,HPV 疫苗的知晓率较高与积极态度之间存在不匹配,同时HPV知识有限与信息不足的感知并存。基于学校的疫苗接种应与重复的、适合年龄的教育相结合,包括女孩、家长和卫生工作者。

title: Heterologous Antigen Regimen and Bicistronic DNA Vaccination Targeting HPV16 E5 and E7 Oncoproteins: Immunoinformatics and Preclinical Antitumor Efficacy
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus, particularly HPV16, is a major cause of cervical cancer and orogenital malignancies. Therapeutic DNA vaccines targeting viral oncoproteins represent a promising strategy to induce antitumor immune responses. However, the impact of antigen combinations in bicistronic vectors and the immunization sequence on therapeutic efficacy remains poorly understood. Thus, this study aimed to characterize in silico previously described E5CP and E7CP vaccines, develop a new bicistronic construct, and evaluate its antitumor efficacy under different immunization regimens in vivo. The constructs were initially characterized regarding predicted physicochemical, immunological, and structural properties, followed by molecular confirmation of plasmid construction and qualitative assessment of transcript detection after transient transfection. In vivo, C57BL/6 mice bearing C3 tumors were immunized with five different regimens combining the monocistronic or bicistronic constructs. At the endpoint, tumors and spleens were collected for histopathological and immunological analyses. The results showed that regimens using the bicistronic construct or including E5 in the first dose were associated with lower mean tumor volumes or delayed tumor growth compared to the control groups. Histopathological and immunophenotypic changes were variable among regimens, and an exploratory analysis suggested an association between lower nitric oxide levels and smaller tumor volumes. Therefore, the order of antigen administration and the use of bicistronic constructs warrant further investigation as strategies that could be optimized to improve the therapeutic efficacy of HPV DNA vaccines.
authors: Keyla Aparecida Alves de Sá Carneiro Melo

abstract_zh: 高危型人乳头瘤病毒,特别是HPV16,是导致宫颈癌和口腔生殖道恶性肿瘤的主要原因。针对病毒癌蛋白的治疗性DNA 疫苗是一种诱导抗肿瘤免疫应答的有前景策略。然而,双顺反子媒介中抗原组合的影响以及免疫接种顺序对治疗效果的影响仍不明确。因此,本研究旨在对之前描述的E5CP和E7CP 疫苗进行计算机模拟分析,开发一种新的双顺反子构建体,并在体内不同免疫接种方案下评估其抗肿瘤功效。首先对构建体进行了预测的理化、免疫学和结构特性的分析,随后通过分子确认了质粒构建,并在瞬时转染后对转录产物进行了定性评估。在体内实验中,携带C3肿瘤的C57BL/6小鼠接受了五种不同的免疫接种方案,这些方案结合了单顺反子或双顺反子构建体。在实验终点时,收集了肿瘤和脾脏样本进行组织病理学和免疫学分析。结果显示,使用双顺反子构建体或在第一剂中包含E5的接种方案与对照组相比,与较低的平均肿瘤体积或延迟的肿瘤生长相关。不同接种方案在组织病理学和免疫表型变化方面存在差异,探索性分析表明较低的硝酸一氧化氮水平与较小的肿瘤体积之间存在关联。因此,抗原接种顺序和双顺反子构建体的使用值得进一步研究,作为可能优化以提高HPV DNA 疫苗治疗效果的策略。

title: NavDx (ctHPVDNA) recurrence detection in surgically treated human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV+)-positivity in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is a favorable prognostic indicator though 10–25% of patients will experience progressive disease within 3 years of treatment. This project assesses the validity of circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance in patients following definitive surgical treatment. A retrospective review of patients with HPV+ OPSCC treated with definitive resection at a single institution between 2020 and 2023 was performed. Patients underwent standard post treatment imaging (CT neck and chest and/or PET/CT). ctHPVDNA samples were also collected. Imaging response was assessed via NI-RADS (Neck Imaging Reporting and Data System) risk classification and independently reviewed. The cohort included 16 patients (15 primary, 1 recurrent): 81% males; median age 58; 56% never smokers, 38% former smokers, 6% current smokers; 63% tonsil primary, 31% BOT; 38% T1, 19% T2, 44% Tx; 0% N0, 25% N1, 38% N2a, 31% N2b, 0% N2c, 6% N3 (AJCC 7th edition). Four patients (25%) experienced biopsy-proven recurrence (13% locoregional, 13% distant) with a median time to recurrence of 14 months (range 3–42). NI-RADS suggested 4 locoregional recurrences (1 true positive, 3 false positive) yielding 50% sensitivity, 75% specificity, 25% PPV, 90% NPV. ctHPVDNA identified 2 locoregional events, and 2 distant events (4 true positive, 0 false positive) yielding 100% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, 100%. Surveillance ctHPVDNA more accurately identified recurrences with minimal false positives compared to post-treatment imaging, which may limit the need for repeat imaging and unwarranted salvage operations which increase patient worry, morbidity, and financial toxicity.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the recurrence detection in surgically treated human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) using circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance. The central question is whether ctHPVDNA is a more accurate method for identifying recurrences compared to standard post-treatment imaging.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes a retrospective review of patients with HPV+ OPSCC who underwent definitive resection at a single institution between 2020 and 2023. ctHPVDNA samples were collected alongside standard post-treatment imaging (CT neck and chest and/or PET/CT). Imaging response was assessed via NI-RADS risk classification and independently reviewed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ctHPVDNA surveillance more accurately identified recurrences with minimal false positives compared to post-treatment imaging. This suggests that ctHPVDNA could potentially reduce the need for repeat imaging and unnecessary salvage operations, thereby decreasing patient worry, morbidity, and financial toxicity.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Post-treatment imaging via NI-RADS had 50% sensitivity and 75% specificity, with 25% false positives. ctHPVDNA showed 100% sensitivity and specificity, but the evidence is limited to a single institution and a small cohort of 16 patients. There is no mention of long-term outcomes or broader applicability.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to validate the utility of ctHPVDNA surveillance in larger, multi-institutional cohorts and to assess its long-term effectiveness. Additionally, studies should explore the integration of ctHPVDNA into routine clinical practice for recurrence monitoring in HPV-associated OPSCC.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the use of circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance for detecting recurrence in surgically treated human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). A retrospective study of 16 patients (2020–2023) found that ctHPVDNA identified all recurrences with 100% sensitivity and specificity, whereas post-treatment imaging via NI-RADS had 50% sensitivity and 75% specificity. The findings suggest that ctHPVDNA may offer more accurate recurrence detection with fewer false positives, potentially reducing the need for repeat imaging and unnecessary salvage procedures. However, the evidence is limited to a single institution and small cohort, highlighting the need for larger, multi-center studies to confirm these results and assess long-term clinical utility.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ctHPVDNA 监测在检测复发方面比术后治疗影像学更为准确,且假阳性较少。这表明ctHPVDNA可能减少重复影像学检查和不必要的挽救性手术,从而降低患者的焦虑、发病率和经济负担。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 术后治疗影像学通过NI-RADS评估具有50%的灵敏度和75%的特异性,假阳性率为25%。ctHPVDNA表现出100%的灵敏度和特异性,但证据仅限于单一机构和16例患者的队列研究。未提及长期结果或更广泛的应用性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究以验证ctHPVDNA 监测在更大规模、多机构的队列研究中的实用性,并评估其长期效果。此外,应研究ctHPVDNA在HPV相关OPSCC复发监测中的临床整合应用。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the recurrence detection in surgically treated human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) using circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance. The central question is whether ctHPVDNA is a more accurate method for identifying recurrences compared to standard post-treatment imaging.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes a retrospective review of patients with HPV+ OPSCC who underwent definitive resection at a single institution between 2020 and 2023. ctHPVDNA samples were collected alongside standard post-treatment imaging (CT neck and chest and/or PET/CT). Imaging response was assessed via NI-RADS risk classification and independently reviewed.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ctHPVDNA surveillance more accurately identified recurrences with minimal false positives compared to post-treatment imaging. This suggests that ctHPVDNA could potentially reduce the need for repeat imaging and unnecessary salvage operations, thereby decreasing patient worry, morbidity, and financial toxicity.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Post-treatment imaging via NI-RADS had 50% sensitivity and 75% specificity, with 25% false positives. ctHPVDNA showed 100% sensitivity and specificity, but the evidence is limited to a single institution and a small cohort of 16 patients. There is no mention of long-term outcomes or broader applicability.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to validate the utility of ctHPVDNA surveillance in larger, multi-institutional cohorts and to assess its long-term effectiveness. Additionally, studies should explore the integration of ctHPVDNA into routine clinical practice for recurrence monitoring in HPV-associated OPSCC.

title_zh: NavDx (ctHPVDNA)在手术治疗的与人乳头瘤病毒相关的口咽部鳞状细胞癌中复发检测
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV+)-positivity in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is a favorable prognostic indicator though 10–25% of patients will experience progressive disease within 3 years of treatment. This project assesses the validity of circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance in patients following definitive surgical treatment. A retrospective review of patients with HPV+ OPSCC treated with definitive resection at a single institution between 2020 and 2023 was performed. Patients underwent standard post treatment imaging (CT neck and chest and/or PET/CT). ctHPVDNA samples were also collected. Imaging response was assessed via NI-RADS (Neck Imaging Reporting and Data System) risk classification and independently reviewed. The cohort included 16 patients (15 primary, 1 recurrent): 81% males; median age 58; 56% never smokers, 38% former smokers, 6% current smokers; 63% tonsil primary, 31% BOT; 38% T1, 19% T2, 44% Tx; 0% N0, 25% N1, 38% N2a, 31% N2b, 0% N2c, 6% N3 (AJCC 7th edition). Four patients (25%) experienced biopsy-proven recurrence (13% locoregional, 13% distant) with a median time to recurrence of 14 months (range 3–42). NI-RADS suggested 4 locoregional recurrences (1 true positive, 3 false positive) yielding 50% sensitivity, 75% specificity, 25% PPV, 90% NPV. ctHPVDNA identified 2 locoregional events, and 2 distant events (4 true positive, 0 false positive) yielding 100% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, 100%. Surveillance ctHPVDNA more accurately identified recurrences with minimal false positives compared to post-treatment imaging, which may limit the need for repeat imaging and unwarranted salvage operations which increase patient worry, morbidity, and financial toxicity.

title: Human Papillomavirus Prevalence and Genotype Distribution in Unvaccinated Women: A Gynaecology and Obstetrics Hospital-Based Retrospective Study in México
abstract: In countries with suboptimal vaccination coverage, human papillomavirus (HPV) genital infections remain a public health problem. Furthermore, the prevalence of specific HPV genotypes in unvaccinated women is uncertain. Therefore, this study aimed to retrospectively evaluate HPV prevalence and genotype distribution among unvaccinated women attending a gynaecology and obstetrics hospital in Mexico, and to establish potential associations between HPV infection and the different pathologies affecting unvaccinated women. A single-centre, retrospective analysis of 347 unvaccinated women who underwent gynaecological examination and had an HPV test was conducted. HPV genotypes in cervical cells were determined using the CLART HPV4 system, which can detect 35 HPV genotypes. Overall, 124 (35.73%) women tested positive for HPV, which included single- and multiple-genotype infections. Oncogenic, high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotypes were detected in 74.19% of the HPV-positive women. Ranked by prevalence, HPV59 was the most frequent, followed by HPV16, HPV39, HPV31, and HPV42. Out of the 11 HR-HPV genotypes identified, 6 are targeted by the nonavalent HPV vaccine. In conclusion, this study reports the prevalence of HPV infection among unvaccinated women attending a gynaecological and obstetric centre and demonstrates that HR-HPV genotypes are the most prevalent in this population. These data may facilitate the design of organised screening and vaccination programmes to reduce genital infection and cervical cancer burden in México.

source_records.abstract: In countries with suboptimal vaccination coverage, human papillomavirus (HPV) genital infections remain a public health problem. Furthermore, the prevalence of specific HPV genotypes in unvaccinated women is uncertain. Therefore, this study aimed to retrospectively evaluate HPV prevalence and genotype distribution among unvaccinated women attending a gynaecology and obstetrics hospital in Mexico, and to establish potential associations between HPV infection and the different pathologies affecting unvaccinated women. A single-centre, retrospective analysis of 347 unvaccinated women who underwent gynaecological examination and had an HPV test was conducted. title: Feasibility and acceptability of self-sampling for human papillomavirus (HPV) screening in a rural community in Western Kenya
abstract: Abstract Introduction Cervical cancer (CC) is the leading cause of female related cancer deaths and the second most common cancer affecting women in Africa. Furthermore, over 3000 mortalities are linked to low screening uptake and Kenya currently reports a CC screening rate of 16%. We sought to determine the feasibility and acceptability of “self-collection” for human papillomavirus (HPV testing) in Webuye Sub County, Western Kenya as a method to overcome low CC screening rates to decrease CC mortality. Methods A qualitative descriptive study design was used to collect data from 20 women who attended a rural village “chama” (meeting for health promotion) on the importance of CC screening. Of the 20 women who participated in this study, 15 women completed the self-collection kit when offered at the chama , and 5 women declined self-collection. Data were collected using in-depth interviews. Investigators used a deductive approach , or a priori , analysis of the data by applying predetermined codes derived from the Health Belief Model. Results Overall, women who accepted screening indicated that knowledge about CC motivated them to take and use the Evalyn® Brush self-collection kit. Additionally, women who acknowledged the greatest risk for CC were those who had multiple sexual partners. Women who declined self-collection discussed fear of adverse physical effects, fear of receiving a positive diagnosis, stigma and loss of privacy as the main barriers to CC screening. Fear voiced by women included pain, bruising, and bleeding from the self-collection device, which in this case was an Evalyn® Brush. Perceived benefits included autonomy in conducting self-collection. Peer support at chama reinforced acceptance of self-collection. Conclusions Self-collection may promote autonomy and uptake of HPV screening in low resourced settings.

title: An 11-Year Comprehensive Retrospective Study on the Prevalence and Genotype Distribution of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) in Women and Men in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus
abstract: Background/Objectives: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most widespread sexually transmitted infections (STIs) worldwide. The aim of the present study was to evaluate the prevalence and genotype distribution of HPV in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus. Methods: In the present study, we analysed HPV results recruited from 37 health centres in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus between 2015 and 2025. Briefly, the presence and genotypes of HPV were detected with two different diagnostic kits. Results: A total of 37,458 molecular test results were evaluated in this study. Overall, 9732 (25.98%) individuals who underwent at least one HPV test were positive. The mean age of HPV-positive individuals was 34.87 ± 9.62 years. HPV positivity was higher in women than in men. The highest HPV positivity rate (41.13%) was observed among individuals younger than 25 years. High-risk (HR) HPV accounted for 42.27% of the 9732 HPV-positive individuals identified in this study. The most common HPV genotypes were 16, 18, and 6, respectively. HPV genotypes 42 and 35 were observed more frequently in women than in men, whereas genotypes 39, 59, and 68 were more prevalent in men. HPV 6 and 11 were most observed in individuals younger than 25 years. Multiple-type infections were most frequently observed in individuals younger than 25 years. Single-type HPV infections were commonly detected in those aged 50–59 years and in individuals over 60 years. Conclusions: These findings contribute to our understanding of epidemiological data on HPV genotype distribution in Türkiye and provide meaningful comparisons across age groups. This study may increase public awareness of HPV infection and help public health authorities develop effective prevention strategies.

title: Association Between Internet Access and Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination Coverage in Brazilian Municipalities: An Ecological Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is the primary strategy for preventing HPV-related cancers, yet vaccination coverage (VC) remains uneven worldwide. Internet access may affect vaccination adherence, but its relationship with HPV VC at the population level is poorly understood. Therefore, we aim to describe the distribution of HPV VC and its association with household internet access across Brazilian municipalities and macro-regions, by sex and year. Methods: This ecological study examined the association between household internet access and HPV VC among girls and boys aged 9 to 14 years in Brazilian municipalities between 2022 and 2024. Two analytical approaches were used: (1) Categorical: both variables were dichotomized by their national medians, and prevalence ratios (PR) were estimated by Poisson regression with robust variance; (2) Continuous: VC was modelled in percentage points (p.p.) and internet access in 10-percentage-point increments, using linear regression with robust variance, for all municipalities and stratified by the five Brazilian macro-regions. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic and contextual variables. Results: A total of 5560 municipalities were included. HPV VC was consistently higher among girls, with medians between 83.5% and 85.2% over the three-year period, than among boys, between 51.9% and 73.6%. The median proportion of internet access was 81.0%, and municipalities classified as having high internet access ranged from about 21.0% in the Northeast to 73.4% in the Central-West. In the categorical approach, municipalities with high internet access showed a higher prevalence of high VC only in 2024, among girls (PR 1.09, 95% CI 1.02–1.15) and boys (PR 1.08, 95% CI 1.02–1.15). In the continuous approach, each 10-p.p. increase in internet access was associated with an increase in VC of 0.59 p.p. among girls in 2023 (95% CI 0.12–1.06) and 0.81 p.p. in 2024 (95% CI 0.37–1.25), and of 0.76 p.p. among boys in 2022 (95% CI 0.19–1.33), 0.86 p.p. in 2023 (95% CI 0.25–1.46) and 1.04 p.p. in 2024 (95% CI 0.50–1.58). Stratified analyses showed positive associations in the North and South, and inverse associations among boys in the Southeast region of Brazil. Conclusions: Municipalities with higher internet access showed higher HPV VC, although the association varied across years, sex, and macro-regions. These findings highlight differences in HPV vaccination coverage according to municipal levels of household internet access.

title: Association Between High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Positivity and Ovarian Reserve Markers in Women with Unexplained Oligomenorrhea: A Retrospective Comparative Study
abstract: Aim: to evaluate the association between high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) positivity and ovarian reserve markers, particularly the anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), in reproductive-age women presenting with unexplained oligomenorrhea. Methods: this single-center retrospective comparative study included women aged 25–35 years with unexplained oligomenorrhea, categorized into an HR-HPV-positive group (n = 257) and an HPV-negative control group (n = 1164). Ovarian reserve was assessed using serum AMH, basal follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), estradiol (E2), and antral follicle count (AFC), with AMH measured irrespective of cycle day and other hormones on cycle days 2–5, while AFC was determined by transvaginal ultrasonography. Clinical and lifestyle variables were recorded, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with low AMH (<0.5 ng/mL). Results: the groups were comparable in age, body mass index, and parity. AMH was lower in HR-HPV-positive women than in controls (median 2.2 [IQR 1.0–3.8] vs. 2.7 [1.5–4.4] ng/mL; p < 0.001), as was AFC (10 [8–13] vs. 11 [9–14]; p < 0.001); the absolute differences were small (Cohen’s d ≤ 0.19). Low AMH was approximately twofold more frequent among HR-HPV-positive women (11.7% vs. 6.3%), and age (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.26–1.47) and HR-HPV positivity (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.24–3.47) were independently associated with low AMH; the association persisted at an alternative threshold of <1.1 ng/mL (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.57–3.23). Conclusion: HR-HPV positivity was associated with lower AMH and AFC values in women with unexplained oligomenorrhea. These findings indicate a group-level association rather than a causal relationship and require confirmation in prospective studies incorporating HPV persistence and reproductive outcomes.

Methods: this single-center retrospective comparative study included women aged 25–35 years with unexplained oligomenorrhea, categorized into an HR-HPV-positive group (n = 257) and an HPV-negative control group (n = 1164). Ovarian reserve was assessed using serum AMH, basal follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), estradiol (E2), and antral follicle count (AFC), with AMH measured irrespective of cycle day and other hormones on cycle days 2–5, while AFC was determined by transvaginal ultrasonography. Clinical and lifestyle variables were recorded, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with low AMH (<0.5 ng/mL). Results: the groups were comparable in age, body mass index, and parity. AMH was lower in HR-HPV-positive women than in controls (median 2.2 [IQR 1.0–3.8] vs. 2.7 [1.5–4.4] ng/mL; p < 0.001), as was AFC (10 [8–13] vs. 11 [9–14]; p < 0.001); the absolute differences were small (Cohen’s d ≤ 0.19). Low AMH was approximately twofold more frequent among HR-HPV-positive women (11.7% vs. 6.3%), and age (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.26–1.47) and HR-HPV positivity (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.24–3.47) were independently associated with low AMH; the association persisted at an alternative threshold of <1.1 ng/mL (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.57–3.23). Conclusion: HR-HPV positivity was associated with lower AMH and AFC values in women with unexplained oligomenorrhea. These findings indicate a group-level association rather than a causal relationship and require confirmation in prospective studies incorporating HPV persistence and reproductive outcomes.

title: Cytology, High-Risk HPV Genotyping, and Histology in Cervical Pathology: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cervical cancer prevention relies on cytology, high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing, and histological confirmation, but these modalities may disagree. We quantified test concordance and determinants of CIN2+ in a specialized gynecologic referral cohort with very low HPV vaccination coverage. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 172 women evaluated for suspected or established cervical pathology between 2022 and 2024. Of these, 160 had a definitive HPV result and 130 had histology; histology-based performance analyses used complete cases and are conditional on biopsy verification. title: Factors associated with high-grade cervical dysplasia in colposcopy patients: the primary role of isolated HPV 16 positivity
abstract: Background Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related fatalities among women globally. Implementing personalized follow-up strategies is crucial for effective prevention of cervical cancer. The present investigation sought to delineate risk factors associated with the development of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) in patients undergoing colposcopy through an analysis of colposcopy indications and histopathological outcomes. Methods This retrospective study included 394 patients aged 30–65 years who underwent colposcopy at Bandırma Onyedi Eylül University Faculty of Medicine Hospital between June 2022 and January 2025 due to high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HR-HPV) positivity, abnormal cervical cytology, or persistent clinical suspicion. The indications for colposcopy, histopathology results, and demographic characteristics such as age and smoking status were analyzed. Results The mean age of the patients was 44.5 ± 10.9 years. The primary indication for colposcopy was observed to be isolated HPV 16 positivity, which accounted for 28% ( n = 112) of cases. Histopathological evaluation showed no cervical dysplasia in 47.3% ( n = 186), CIN I in 34.5% ( n = 136), CIN II–III in 17.7% ( n = 70), and cervical carcinoma in 0.5% ( n = 2). Isolated HPV 16 positivity remained a significant independent predictor of CIN II–III after adjustment for age and smoking status (Adjusted Odds Ratio (AOR) = 2.388, 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 1.387–4.112, p < 0.05). Conclusions Isolated HPV 16 positivity was independently associated with an approximately 2.4-fold increase in the odds of CIN II–III after adjustment for age and smoking status. This finding reinforces the central role of HPV 16 in identifying women at higher risk for high-grade cervical dysplasia and supports its prioritization in risk-based colposcopy and follow-up strategies.

title: The Relationship Between Interferon Status and HPV Infection in Patients with Oral Epithelial Dysplasia: An Observational Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Oral potentially malignant diseases (OPMDs) with signs of epithelial dysplasia are characterized by a high risk of malignancy. However, there are still no algorithms for their early diagnosis and prediction, due to the many possible predisposing factors, including human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and decreased immunity. There is a need to assess the relationship between the manifestations of oral epithelial dysplasia (OED), HPV invasion in the oral cavity, and interferon status to improve the identification and characterization of patients with different degrees of dysplasia. Methods: This study was designed and reported with reference to the STROBE checklist. The study aimed to assess the association between interferon status and HPV invasion in patients with OED. As per the inclusion and exclusion criteria, this observational study included 180 patients with histologically confirmed oral epithelial dysplasia associated with leukoplakia or oral lichen planus. Interferon (IFN) status was assessed by measuring serum interferon activity, spontaneous interferon production, IFN-α/β, and IFN-γ activity in peripheral blood. HPV DNA was detected and genotyped in biopsy specimens using polymerase chain reaction. Results: HPV-positive patients demonstrated significantly lower IFN-α/β and IFN-γ activity compared with HPV-negative patients (p < 0.001). Severe OED was more frequently observed in HPV-positive individuals, whereas mild dysplasia predominated among HPV-negative patients (p < 0.05). Interferon activity progressively decreased with increasing dysplasia severity, with the lowest IFN-α/β and IFN-γ activity detected in patients with severe dysplasia (p < 0.001 and p < 0.05, respectively). A significant positive correlation between IFN-α/β and IFN-γ activity was identified in patients with moderate dysplasia (p = 0.003). Multivariate binary logistic regression analysis demonstrated that HPV positivity (adjusted OR = 4.62, 95% CI: 2.18–9.79; p < 0.001) and reduced IFN-α/β activity (adjusted OR = 1.34 per 10-unit decrease, 95% CI: 1.14–1.58; p < 0.001) were independently associated with severe dysplasia. The multivariable model demonstrated acceptable discriminatory ability for identifying patients with severe dysplasia (AUC = 0.736), with a sensitivity of 89.4% and a specificity of 56.1%. Conclusions: The findings suggest that HPV-associated OED is linked to reduced interferon status, particularly lower IFN-α/β and IFN-γ activity in more severe dysplastic lesions. Combined assessment of interferon status and HPV detection may help identify patients at higher risk of severe OED.

title: Rastreamento do Câncer Cervical e a Relação com a Vacinação Contra Human Papillomavirus (HPV)
abstract: Este estudo visa analisar evidências científicas sobre os impactos da vacinação contra o Human Papillomavirus (HPV) na incidência de câncer do colo do útero. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa com análise qualitativa. A coleta de dados foi realizada em três bases de dados, por meio dos Descritores em Ciências da Saúde (DeCS) combinados com o operador booleano OR. A tipagem por biologia molecular do Human Papillomavirus demonstrou maior sensibilidade na detecção de lesões em comparação ao exame citopatológico. Ademais, mulheres vacinadas apresentaram menores chances de desenvolver câncer cervical em relação às não vacinadas. Conclui-se que a vacinação e a tipagem viral modificam a necessidade e a periodicidade do rastreamento, permitindo intervalos mais amplos e maior precisão. Apesar da redução da mortalidade entre jovens, o rastreamento contínuo permanece essencial em mulheres de faixas etárias mais avançadas. Destaca-se a importância de políticas públicas que integrem vacinação, rastreamento e ações educativas em saúde.

title: HPV6/11 Persistence and Treatment-Associated Immune Remodeling in Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis: A Cross-Cohort Transcriptomic Analysis
abstract: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), caused mainly by human papillomavirus types 6 and 11 (HPV6/11), can persist despite the absence of recognized systemic immunodeficiency. We reanalyzed three transcriptomic datasets using the same predefined immune-gene programs: paired papilloma and autologous laryngeal mucosa from 12 patients, single-cell RNA sequencing from papillomas of four RRP donors and pharyngopalatine mucosa from three controls, and paired papilloma samples from 17 patients before and after INO-3107, a DNA immunotherapy encoding HPV6/11 antigens and interleukin-12. In untreated tissue, cluster of differentiation 8 (CD8)- and natural killer (NK)-associated cytotoxic program scores were lower and the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) suppressive program score was higher, reproducing findings from the same cohort. The lower cytotoxic pattern was not reproduced within the recovered combined T-cell and NK-cell population, although no single-cell comparison remained significant after correction for multiple testing. After INO-3107, CD8- and NK-associated cytotoxic, T helper 1 (Th1)/interferon gamma (IFN-γ), and C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)-associated trafficking program scores increased significantly, whereas TGF-β and M2-like suppressive programs showed no comparable statistically supported change. Together, these findings show that different components of the local immune response do not change in parallel and support a model of selective treatment-associated immune remodeling. This pattern may inform future biomarker and combination-treatment studies.

title: Health Workers' Perspectives on Caregiver Barriers to Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccine Uptake in Selected Health Facilities in Edo State, Nigeria: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is highly effective in preventing HPV-related disease, yet uptake remains uneven in many low- and middle-income settings. This study explored caregiver-related barriers to HPV vaccine uptake as reported by immunisation-clinic health workers in selected health facilities in Edo State, Nigeria. Methods: A qualitative cross-sectional study was conducted in 2024 among 11 health workers purposively recruited from immunisation clinics in three hospitals in Benin City. Individual in-depth interviews were conducted with a structured interview guide by a trained moderator. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, independently checked for accuracy, and analysed using Braun and Clarke's thematic approach with MAXQDA 2022. Thematic saturation was reached by the eleventh interview. Results: Participants described low and inconsistent HPV vaccine utilisation at their facilities. Reported barriers included limited awareness, misconceptions and culturally mediated concerns, historical out-of-pocket costs, and intermittent vaccine availability. Participants also described facility-level or transitional gaps in routine integration during Nigeria's 2024 phased HPV vaccine rollout. Suggested strategies included community mobilisation, sustained health education, health-worker training, reliable vaccine availability, and removal of financial barriers. Conclusion: The findings indicate that HPV vaccine uptake in the study setting was shaped by interacting informational, sociocultural, financial, and service-delivery barriers. Because the interviews occurred during a period of national programme transition, reports of payment and non-inclusion should be interpreted as local or historical experiences rather than as current national policy. Strengthening communication, community engagement, workforce capacity, and reliable routine vaccine delivery may support sustained uptake.

title: Longitudinal changes in circulating HPV16 DNA during chemoradiotherapy and their association with tumor burden in oropharyngeal cancer
abstract: Circulating HPV DNA has been investigated as a biomarker in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, but its longitudinal behavior during chemoradiotherapy remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated dynamic changes in plasma HPV16 ctDNA and their association with tumor burden and clinical outcomes. In this prospective study, patients with p16-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma underwent serial plasma HPV16 ctDNA measurements using droplet digital PCR before, during, and after definitive chemoradiotherapy. ctDNA levels were analyzed in relation to tumor volume, treatment response, and recurrence. Total 61 patients with p16-positive oropharyngeal cancer were enrolled. Among 42 patients with HPV16-positive tumors, baseline HPV16 ctDNA levels were at or above the predefined limit of detection (LoD) in 26 patients (61.9%). Three distinct clearance patterns were observed: continuous decline (Type I, n = 16), transient increase followed by decline (Type II, n = 12), and persistently below-LoD levels (Type III, n = 14). Maximum ctDNA levels were significantly correlated with nodal tumor volume (Type I: r = 0.57, p = 0.02; Type II: r = 0.61, p = 0.03), but not with primary tumor volume. title: Multi-scale Transcriptional Characterization of HPV16 and HPV18 in Cervical Cancer: Host Pathway Alterations and Links With Viral Gene Expression Programs
abstract: High-risk HPV is central to cervical carcinogenesis, but whether individual genotypes drive distinct tumor biology or converge on a shared oncogenic state remains unclear. Profiling viral and host gene expression across two independent cohorts (n = 93; 76 HPV16, 17 HPV18), we show that HPV16- and HPV18-associated cervical cancers differ in host transcriptional programs. A 55-gene signature discriminated the two genotypes, and 293 genes were concordantly differentially expressed across cohorts. Pathway and transcription-factor activity inference organized these differences along genotype-specific axes: HPV16 tumors were enriched for epithelial polarity and RTK-RAS-MAPK signatures, with elevated inferred CDX2 regulon activity, a transcription factor not normally active in cervical epithelium, suggesting an aberrant lineage-identity program not previously linked to this genotype. HPV18 tumors instead showed metabolic reprogramming and inflammatory signaling (STAT3, HIF1A), alongside reduced CASP8 and increased FDX1 expression, a pattern consistent with sensitization to immunogenic cell death. Both genotypes also organized along a continuum of early-to-late viral gene expression correlating with distinct host pathways: extracellular-matrix and translation-related in HPV16, interferon/antiviral and cell-cycle/mitochondrial in HPV18, indicating that viral transcriptional state associates with host biology beyond genotype alone. These results point to candidate genotype-specific vulnerabilities that merit functional validation.

title: Clinical and Anamnestic Characteristics and Risk Factors for the Progression of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia in Women of Reproductive Age: A Comparative Analysis in Regions with Different Socioeconomic and Cultural Conditions (The Case of Astrakhan and Bukhara)
abstract: Purpose of the article. To evaluate clinical and anamnestic characteristics, risk factors for cervical dysplasia progression, and colposcopic markers of CIN I–III in women residing in regions with different socioeconomic and cultural conditions. Materials and Methods. Пациентки (20-45лет) с CIN были разделены на две группы: жительницы Астрахани (111 человек) (Россия) и Бухары (113 человек) (Узбекистан). Каждая группа была разделена на три подгруппы в зависимости от степени CIN. Проводилось обследование, включая: ВПЧ‐тестирование (16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59 типы); жидкостную цитологию мазка с шейки матки; оценку биоценоза влагалища, кольпоскопию. Статистическая обработка данных выполнена с использованием пакетов Statistica12.0 и SPSSStatistics. Regional differences were identified: in the Russian group, women who smoked were more common (28.8%) and patients using hormonal contraception (43.2%) (in the CIN III subgroup (90.6%)); In the Uzbek group, housewives predominated (44.2% (among patients with CIN III - 71.9%) with low adherence to preventive examinations (38.1% had not visited a gynecologist for more than 5 years). Key risk factors for CIN progression were established: infection with highly oncogenic HPV types and coinfection with several types (more often with CIN III); dysbiotic disorders of the vagina (more often with CIN II-CIN III); a history of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and previous treatment of the cervix (more often with severe forms of CIN). Colposcopy demonstrated a fairly high diagnostic value between the severity of visual changes (acetowhite epithelium, mosaic, puncturation) and the degree of dysplasia.

title: Human Papilloma Virus Genotyping in Women with Condyloma Acuminata: A Cross-sectional, Hospital-based Study
abstract: Abstract Background: Condyloma acuminata (CA), caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), is a prevalent sexually transmitted disease. Multiple HPV genotypes are implicated in causation, with types 6 and 11 being the most frequently associated. Aims: To study the HPV genotype in women with CA with respect to high-risk (HR) and low-risk variants, and in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) positive and negative hosts. Methods: This prospective, cross-sectional study was conducted at three centers, including Manipal, Bangalore, and Guntur, from February 2021 to March 2024 (CTRI 2020/02/023218). Adult females aged 18–65 years, attending respective Dermatology departments, who were clinically diagnosed as CA, with a positive acetowhitening test, were included. HPV genotyping was performed on tissue samples. Results: A total of 79 women were included in the study. A total of 10 HPV genotypes were found in the 79 cases, among which HPV-6 (70.89%) and HPV-11 (22.78%) were most prevalent. HPV-16 was the most common HR HPV. Infection with a single HPV genotype ( n = 59) was higher than that with multiple HPV genotypes ( n = 13) ( P < 0.001). The prevalence rates of single and multiple HPV infections differed among the various age groups. Only three women were HIV positive. Limitations: This study had a small sample size from three centers, and a very low incidence of HIV positivity, due to which meaningful comparison between HIV positive and HIV-negative groups was impractical. Conclusion: HPV-6 and HPV-11 are still the predominant genotypes causing CA in Indian women, the leading HR genotype being HPV-16. Single HPV infections were more common, particularly in younger women.

A total of 10 HPV genotypes were found in the 79 cases, among which HPV-6 (70.89%) and HPV-11 (22.78%) were most prevalent. HPV-16 was the most common HR HPV. Infection with a single HPV genotype ( n = 59) was higher than that with multiple HPV genotypes ( n = 13) ( P < 0.001). The prevalence rates of single and multiple HPV infections differed among the various age groups. Only three women were HIV positive. Limitations: This study had a small sample size from three centers, and a very low incidence of HIV positivity, due to which meaningful comparison between HIV positive and HIV-negative groups was impractical. Conclusion: HPV-6 and HPV-11 are still the predominant genotypes causing CA in Indian women, the leading HR genotype being HPV-16. Single HPV infections were more common, particularly in younger women.

title: A multi-centre study on cervical cancer screening reveals population-related impact on cervical intraepithelial neoplasia rate
abstract: Objective To conduct a three-year cervical cancer screen in Zhejiang, Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia and analyse clinical and population data to identify possible improvements to the screening protocol. Methods A standard protocol including human papillomavirus (HPV) detection, cytology test, colposcopy, and histopathology inspection was adapted for the screening. Additional HPV genotyping was performed for participants in Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia. Results 12,086 women were included in this study, and 178 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) were identified. Detailed analyses on features of age, region, ethnicity, and origin showed a notable correlation between age strata and high-grade CIN rates. Moreover, apart from HPV16/18, other HPV types such as HPV33, HPV52, and HPV58 were found to be enriched in high-grade CIN cases, as was repeat positivity. Conclusions Our results suggest that age, HPV16, and ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) are prominent exploratory predictors for CIN2+ detection, and HPV33, 52, and 58 may pose higher risks than other non-HPV16/18 types. Future studies incorporating prospective effectiveness and health-economic evaluation are required to validate the clinical utility of these predictors.

title: Frequency of seropositivity ofsyphillis and HIV in patients with anogenital warts
abstract: Background Anogenital warts (condylomata acuminata) are benign, sexually transmitted proliferative lesions of the anogenital skin and mucosa caused predominantly by low-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) types, particularly HPV 6 and 11. Aim of present study is to determine the frequency of seropositivity of syphilis and HIV in patients with anogenital warts. Objective To determine the frequency of seropositivity of syphilis and HIV in patients with anogenital warts. Methods One sixty patients were enrolled in the study. Clinical examination of anogenital area in the presence of suitable chaperone where required, were carried out in all patients. Laboratory test like TPHA for syphilis and HIV by ELISA were done in every patient from a single reference laboratory to avoid variability was test results. All patients were managed as per standard protocols. All the data was processed by SPSS v26.0. Frequency and percentages were used for categorical parameters. Chi square test was applied in which P-valve <.05 was considered significant. Results Gender distribution of the patients showed that 79.4% (n=127) were male whereas 20.6 %( n=33) were females. The distribution of sexual preferences was as follows: 18.8% (n=30) of participants were homosexual, 66.9% (n=107) were heterosexual, and 14.4% (n=23) were bisexual. The frequency of HIV seropositivity was 8.1% (n=13), while the frequency of syphilis seropositivity was 3.1% (n=5). Conclusion The study demonstrated the presence of both HIV and syphilis seropositivity among patients with anogenital warts, highlighting the importance of appropriate screening for sexually transmitted infections in this population. The findings should be interpreted in the context of the characteristics of the study population and the local epidemiological setting.

title: The Association of Oncogenic HPV Strains with Colposcopic and Histopathological Parameters of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is among the most prevalent malignancies impacting women, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The prompt identification of precancerous lesions is essential, as early care may avert the development of aggressive malignancy. OBJECTIVE: To assess the correlation between oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) strains and colposcopic and histological characteristics of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to December 2024 at the cervical precancerous lesion clinic of Al-Yarmouk Teaching Hospital, Baghdad. Thirty-seven women with abnormal Pap smear results were enrolled in the study. All participants underwent colposcopic examination followed by cervical biopsy for histopathological assessment. High-risk HPV genotypes were detected using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) on liquid-based cytology samples. RESULTS: High-risk HPV infection was detected in most cases, with HPV genotype 56 being the most frequently identified. A subset of patients showed multiple HPV infections. HPV testing demonstrated higher sensitivity for detecting high-grade CIN lesions compared with Pap smear and colposcopy. A significant positive correlation was observed between HPV infection and colposcopic abnormalities. CONCLUSION: Women with abnormal cervical cytology often had oncogenic HPV infections, and HPV testing was more accurate in finding high-grade CIN lesions. These results support the use of HPV testing in addition to standard screening techniques. They also stress the need for bigger multicenter studies to validate the distribution of genotypes and the effectiveness of screening.

title: Risk stratification of high-grade lesions in atypical glandular cells, not otherwise specified: a refined model incorporating HPV phylogenetic clades and multiple HPV infection
abstract: To investigate the age, distribution of HPV phylogenetic clades and multiple infections in atypical glandular cells, not otherwise specified (AGC-NOS), and to develop a refined risk prediction model. We retrospectively analyzed 588 patients diagnosed with AGC-NOS at the International Peace Maternal and Child Health Hospital, School of Medicine, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, between January 2019 and December 2023. All patients underwent liquid-based cytology testing and high-risk HPV (hrHPV) testing for 14 genotypes, followed by histopathologic evaluation. Precancerous or worse lesions were identified in 9.5% of patients (56/588), and the overall hrHPV positivity rate was 17.7% (104/588). The Alpha-9 and Alpha-7 clades were significantly enriched in the outcome group compared with the non-outcome group (19.6% vs. 1.5%, respectively). In multivariable analysis, Alpha-7 (OR = 20.43, 95% CI: 7.22–60.07), Alpha-9 (OR = 3.41, 95% CI: 1.43–7.57), and age (OR = 1.04 per year, 95% CI: 1.01–1.07) were independent predictors. The model showed acceptable discrimination (AUC = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.66–0.82) and good calibration. Observed lesion rates in the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups were 4.5% (8/176), 8.2% (30/364), and 37.5% (18/48), respectively ( P for trend = 6.7 × 10−8). A model incorporating HPV phylogenetic clades, age, infection multiplicity, and AGC subtype provided preliminary evidence of potential value for risk stratification in AGC-NOS. The Alpha-7 clade was the strongest independent predictor. Pending external validation, this approach may support more individualized management of patients with AGC-NOS.

title: Which Days Of The Menstrual Cycle Are The Most Appropriate For Cervicovaginal Smear And High-Risk HPV Tests?
abstract: Aim: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of menstrual cycle timing on cervicovaginal smear cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) results in premenopausal women.Materials and Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 1.096 premenopausal women under HR-HPV follow-up between March 2024 and March 2025. Patients were categorized into postmenstrual (n = 561) and premenstrual (n = 535) groups based on the timing of sample collection. Cytological classifications, HR-HPV genotypes, and colposcopy results were compared between groups. Statistical analyses included Chi-square, Fisher’s exact, and with p 0.05). No difference was observed in colposcopic outcomes between the two phases.Conclusion: Menstrual cycle timing does not significantly influence cervicovaginal smear adequacy, cytological interpretation, or HR-HPV detection in premenopausal women. Cervical screening can be safely performed at any time outside active menstruation. Removing unnecessary timing restrictions may enhance screening compliance and accessibility.

title: Một số yếu tố liên quan đến nhiễm Human Papillomavirus nguy cơ cao ở phụ nữ 21-49 tuổi tại Hà Nội và thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, giai đoạn 2023-2024 Factors associated with high-risk Human Papillomavirus infection
abstract: Nhiễm Human papillomavirus (HPV) nguy cơ cao là yếu tố hàng gây ung thư cổ tử cung (UTCTC). Việcphát hiện sớm nhiễm HPV nguy cơ cao sẽ giúp phát hiện, theo dõi và điều trị sớm UTCTC. Nghiên cứunhằm mô tả một số yếu tố liên quan đến nhiễm HPV nguy cơ cao ở phụ nữ 21 – 49 tuổi tại Hà Nội và thànhphố Hồ Chí Minh. Thiết kế nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang trên 528 phụ nữ từ 21 - 49 tuổi, khám phụ khoa vàxét nghiệm HPV tại các Phòng khám/Bệnh viện phụ sản trên địa bàn Hà Nội và Thành phố Hồ Chí Minhtừ năm 2023 – 2024. Kết quả phân tích đơn biến cho thấy nhiễm HPV nguy cơ cao có mối liên quan có ýnghĩa thống kê với nghề nghiệp (nông dân, làm tự do), tuổi có kinh lần đầu sớm, đã từng sàng lọc UTCTC,tiền sử viêm CTC, viêm âm hộ, khí hư bất thường, CTC bị tổn thương (viêm CTC, nang Naboth, polypCTC). Phân tích hồi quy đa biến cho thấy tuổi có kinh lần đầu, tiền sử sàng lọc UTCTC, khí hư bất thườnglà các yếu tố độc lập liên quan đến nhiễm HPV nguy cơ cao. Chính vì vậy, nghiên cứu khuyến nghị nhữngphụ nữ trong độ tuổi 21 – 49 nên thực hiện xét nghiệm HPV nguy cơ cao, sàng lọc UTCTC định kỳ, đặcbiệt những người tuổi có kinh lần đầu sớm, khí hư bất thường.

title: Investigation of the Effect of Web-Assisted Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) Education on the Knowledge Level and Health Beliefs Regarding HPV Infection and Vaccination of Female Employees of a University
abstract: In this study, the effect of web-based Human Papillomavirus (HPV) education given to female employees of a university on their knowledge and health beliefs about HPV infection and vaccination was examined. The study was designed using an experimental method. The population of the study consisted of women working at a foundation university in Istanbul. The sample consisted of 45 women who participated in the pre-test and post-test. The data were obtained using a demographic information form, "Human Papilloma Virus-Knowledge Scale" and "Health Belief Model Scale on Human Papilloma Virus Infection and Vaccination". 93.3% of the women had not received HPV vaccination and 48.8% stated that they had not received HPV vaccination because they did not consider themselves at risk. It was determined that there was no significant difference between the pre-test and post-test in the sub-dimensions of Perception of Benefit (p=0.579), Perception of Sensitivity (p=0.332) and Perception of Seriousness (p=0.473) of the Health Belief Model Scale regarding HPV Infection and Vaccination. It was determined that there was a significant difference between the pre-test and post-test in the Perception of Obstacle (p=0.048) sub-dimension and the number of correct answers in the knowledge score (p=0.000); the average number of correct answers. in the perception of obstacle sub-dimension and the post-test were higher. As a result of the research, it is recommended that a face-to-face training model should be preferred instead of web-based training, and training sessions should be repeated at regular intervals.
